translations.text: The Lord spoke to Moses in the wilderness of Sinai, in the tent of testimony, on the first day of the second month in the second year after they had left the land of Egypt, saying:
Take a census of the whole congregation of the Israelites, by their clans and ancestral households, counting every male by name, one by one,
from twenty years old and upward, everyone who can serve in Israel’s army. You and Aaron shall muster them with their forces.
With you there shall be one man from each tribe, each a leader of his ancestral household.
These are the names of the men who shall stand with you: from Reuben, Elizur son of Shedeur;
from Simeon, Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai;
from Judah, Nahshon son of Amminadab;
from Issachar, Nethanel son of Zuar;
from Zebulun, Eliab son of Helon;
from the sons of Joseph: from Ephraim, Elishama son of Ammihud; from Manasseh, Gamaliel son of Pedahzur;
from Benjamin, Abidan son of Gideon;
from Dan, Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai;
from Asher, Pagiel son of Ocran;
from Gad, Elizaphan son of Deuel;
from Naphtali, Ahira son of Enan.
These are the distinguished men of the congregation, leaders of the tribes according to their ancestral households, commanders of thousands in Israel.
Moses and Aaron took these men who had been called by name,

and they assembled the whole congregation on the first day of the second month in the second year. They were enrolled by their clans and ancestral households, counting their names, every male from twenty years old and upward, one by one.
As the Lord commanded Moses, they were enrolled in the wilderness of Sinai.

The sons of Reuben, Israel’s firstborn, were listed by their clans, their divisions, and their ancestral households, counting their names one by one: every male from twenty years old and upward, everyone who could serve in Israel’s army.
Those counted from the tribe of Reuben were forty-six thousand five hundred.

And the sons of Simeon, according to their families, their divisions, and their ancestral houses, by the number of their names, counted individually: every male twenty years old and over who went out to serve in the army.
Those enrolled from the tribe of Simeon numbered fifty-nine thousand three hundred.

The sons of Gad were listed by their clans, their divisions, and their ancestral households, counting their names one by one: every male from twenty years old and upward, everyone who could serve in the army.
Those enrolled from the tribe of Gad numbered forty-five thousand six hundred fifty.

The sons of Judah were listed by their clans, their divisions, and their ancestral households, counting their names one by one: every male from twenty years old and upward, everyone who could serve in the army.
Those counted from the tribe of Judah were seventy-four thousand six hundred.

The sons of Issachar were listed by their clans, their divisions, and their ancestral households, counting their names one by one: every male from twenty years old and upward, everyone who could serve in the army.
Those counted from the tribe of Issachar numbered fifty-four thousand four hundred.

And among the descendants of Zebulun, by their divisions, their clans, and their ancestral households, according to the number of their names, counted individually: every male twenty years old and upward who went out to serve in the army.
Those counted from the tribe of Zebulun numbered fifty-seven thousand four hundred.

And the sons of Joseph, the sons of Ephraim, according to their families, their divisions, and their ancestral houses, by the number of their names, counted individually: every male twenty years old and over who went out to serve in the army.
Those counted from the tribe of Ephraim numbered forty thousand five hundred.

And among the descendants of Manasseh, by their clans, their divisions, and their ancestral households, according to the number of their names, counted individually: every male twenty years old and upward who went out to serve in the army.
Those counted from the tribe of Manasseh numbered thirty-two thousand two hundred.

And among the descendants of Benjamin, by their clans, their divisions, and their ancestral households, according to the number of their names, counted individually: every male twenty years old and upward who went out to serve in the army.
Those counted from the tribe of Benjamin numbered thirty-five thousand four hundred.

And among the descendants of Dan, by their clans, their divisions, and their ancestral households, according to the number of their names, counted individually: every male twenty years old and upward who went out to serve in the army.
Those counted from the tribe of Dan numbered sixty-two thousand seven hundred.

And among the descendants of Asher, by their clans, their divisions, and their ancestral households, according to the number of their names, counted individually: every male twenty years old and upward who went out to serve in the army.
Those counted from the tribe of Asher numbered forty-one thousand five hundred.

And among the descendants of Naphtali, by their clans, their divisions, and their ancestral households, according to the number of their names, counted individually: every male twenty years old and upward who went out to serve in the army.
Those counted from the tribe of Naphtali numbered fifty-three thousand four hundred.
This is the census taken by Moses and Aaron and the leaders of Israel. There were twelve leaders, one man from each clan, according to the tribes of their ancestral households.
And the entire census of the Israelites, with their army, comprised those twenty years old and upward, everyone in Israel who went out to wage war.
And all those included in the census numbered six hundred three thousand five hundred fifty.
But the Levites, from the tribe of their own clan, were not included in the census with the Israelites.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said:
See to it that you do not include the clan of Levi with them in the census, and do not count them among the Israelites.

And you shall put the Levites in charge of the tabernacle of the testimony, all its furnishings, and everything in it. They shall carry the tabernacle and all its furnishings, and they shall serve in it and camp around the tabernacle.
And when the tabernacle moves, the Levites shall take it down, and when the tabernacle is encamped, the Levites shall set it up. Any outsider who approaches it shall die.
And the Israelites shall camp, each man according to his own assigned position and each man according to his own ancestral household, with their army.

But the Levites shall camp around the tabernacle of the testimony before the Lord, so that there may be no sins among the Israelites. And the Levites shall keep watch over the tabernacle of the testimony.
And the Israelites did everything just as the Lord commanded Moses and Aaron; so they did.
And the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron and said:
Each man shall march behind the standard of his own division, according to his ancestral household. The Israelites shall camp according to their camps.
Those who camp foremost, on the eastern side, shall be the division of the camp of Judah, with their forces. The leader of the people of Judah shall be Nahshon son of Amminadab.
His forces, counted at the muster, numbered seventy-four thousand six hundred.
The tribe of Issachar shall camp behind them. The leader of the people of Issachar shall be Nethanel son of Zuar.
His forces, counted at the muster, numbered fifty-four thousand four hundred.
The tribe of Zebulun shall camp beside them. The leader of the people of Zebulun shall be Eliab son of Helon.
His forces, counted at the muster, numbered fifty-seven thousand four hundred.
All those counted at the muster of the camp of Judah numbered one hundred eighty-six thousand four hundred, with their forces. They shall set out first.
The division of the camp of Reuben shall be on the southern side, with their forces. The leader of the people of Reuben shall be Elizur son of Shedeur.
His forces, counted at the muster, numbered forty-six thousand five hundred.
The tribe of Simeon shall camp beside him. The leader of the people of Simeon shall be Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai.
His forces, counted at the muster, numbered fifty-nine thousand three hundred.
The tribe of Gad shall camp beside him. The leader of the people of Gad shall be Elizaphan son of Deuel.
His forces, counted at the muster, numbered forty-five thousand six hundred fifty.
All those counted at the muster of the division of Reuben numbered one hundred fifty-one thousand four hundred fifty, with their forces. They shall set out second.

Then the tabernacle of the testimony shall set out, with the camp of the Levites in the middle of the camps. As they camp, so shall they set out, each following the other according to their leadership.
The division of the camp of Ephraim shall be on the western side, with their forces. The leader of the people of Ephraim shall be Elishama son of Ammihud.
His forces, counted at the muster, numbered forty thousand five hundred.
The tribe of Manasseh shall camp behind them. The leader of the people of Manasseh shall be Gamaliel son of Pedahzur.
His forces, counted at the muster, numbered thirty-two thousand two hundred.
The division of Benjamin shall camp behind them. The leader of the people of Benjamin shall be Abidan son of Gideoni.
His forces, counted at the muster, numbered thirty-five thousand four hundred.
All those counted at the muster of the camp of Ephraim numbered one hundred eight thousand two hundred, with their forces. They shall set out third.
The division of the camp of Dan shall be on the northern side, with their forces. The leader of the people of Dan shall be Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai.
His forces, counted at the muster, numbered sixty-two thousand seven hundred.
The tribe of Asher shall camp beside him, and the leader of the descendants of Asher shall be Pagiel son of Ocran.
His army, those counted in the census, numbered forty-one thousand five hundred.
The tribe of Naphtali shall camp beside him, and the leader of the descendants of Naphtali shall be Ahira son of Enan.
His army, those counted in the census, numbered fifty-three thousand four hundred.
All those counted in the census of the camp of Dan, with their armies, numbered one hundred fifty-seven thousand six hundred. They shall set out last, by their divisions.
This is the census of the Israelites according to their ancestral households: the total count of the camps, with their armies, was six hundred three thousand five hundred fifty.
But the Levites were not counted with them in the census, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
The Israelites did everything just as the Lord had commanded Moses. They camped by their divisions and set out in the same way, each with their own tribe, according to their ancestral households.
These are the descendants of Aaron and Moses on the day when the Lord spoke with Moses on Mount Sinai.
These are the names of Aaron’s sons: Nadab the firstborn, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
These are the names of Aaron’s sons, the anointed priests who were consecrated to serve as priests.

Nadab and Abihu died before the Lord when they offered unauthorized fire before the Lord in the wilderness of Sinai. They had no sons, and Eleazar and Ithamar served as priests alongside Aaron their father.
And the Lord spoke to Moses and said:
Take the tribe of Levi and have them stand before Aaron the priest, and they shall serve him.
They shall carry out his duties and the duties of the Israelites before the tent of testimony, doing the work of the tent.
They shall take care of all the equipment of the tent of testimony and carry out the duties of the Israelites and all the work of the tent.
You shall give the Levites to Aaron your brother and to his sons, the priests. They shall be given as a gift from among the Israelites.

You shall put Aaron and his sons in charge of the tent of testimony, and they shall attend to their priestly duties and everything concerning the altar and everything inside the curtain. Any outsider who approaches shall be put to death.
And the Lord spoke to Moses and said:
And behold, I have taken the Levites from among the Israelites in place of every firstborn who opens the womb among the Israelites. They shall be their ransom, and the Levites shall be mine.

For every firstborn is mine. On the day when I struck down every firstborn in the land of the Egyptians, I consecrated to myself every firstborn in Israel, from humans to livestock. They shall be mine, for I am the Lord.
The Lord spoke with Moses in the wilderness of Sinai and said:
Take a census of the sons of Levi according to their ancestral houses, their divisions, and their families. You shall count every male one month old and over.
Moses and Aaron counted them at the Lord’s word, just as the Lord had commanded them.
These are the sons of Levi by their names: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
These are the names of Gershon’s sons according to their clans: Libni and Shimei.
The sons of Kohath according to their clans were Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel.
The sons of Merari according to their clans were Mahli and Mushi. These are the clans of the Levites according to their ancestral households.
To Gershon belonged the clan of the Libnites and the clan of the Shimeites. These are the clans of Gershon.
Their census counted every male a month old and older; their total was seven thousand five hundred.
These clans of Gershon shall camp behind the tabernacle, on the west side.
The leader of the ancestral house of the clan of Gershon shall be Elisaphan son of Geilai.
The sons of Gershon shall be responsible for the tabernacle, its outer coverings, and the curtains of the tabernacle of testimony,
and the hangings of the courtyard, the curtain at the entrance of the tabernacle, and all the other accessories for its service.
To Kohath belong the clan of Amram, the clan of Izhar, the clan of Hebron, and the clan of Uzziel. These are the clans of Kohath.
The number of all the males one month old and older was eight thousand six hundred. They shall be responsible for the care of the holy things.
The clans of the sons of Kohath shall camp beside the tabernacle, on the south side.
The leader of the ancestral house of the clan of Kohath shall be Elizaphan son of Uzziel.
They shall be responsible for the ark, the table, the lampstand, the altars, the sacred furnishings used in worship, the veil, and all their equipment.
Eleazar son of Aaron the priest shall be chief over the leaders of the Levites, overseeing the care of the holy things.
To Merari belong the clan of Mahli and the clan of Mushi. These are the clans of Merari.
Their enrollment, counting every male one month old and older, was six thousand two hundred.
The leader of the ancestral house of the clan of Merari shall be Zuriel son of Abihail. They shall camp beside the tabernacle, on the north side, and their enrollment.
The sons of Merari shall be responsible for the capitals of the tabernacle, its bars, its pillars, its bases, and all their furnishings and equipment,
and the pillars surrounding the courtyard, their bases, their pegs, and their cords.

Those who camp in front of the tabernacle of testimony, on the east side, shall be Moses and Aaron and his sons. They shall be responsible for the care of the holy things on behalf of the Israelites. Any outsider who approaches shall be put to death.
The total enrollment of the Levites whom Moses and Aaron enrolled at the Lord’s command, according to their clans, counting every male one month old and older, was twenty-two thousand.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said, “Enroll every firstborn male among the Israelites one month old and older, and count them by name.
Take the Levites for me—for I am the Lord—in place of all the firstborn of the Israelites, and the livestock of the Levites in place of the firstborn livestock of the Israelites.”
Moses enrolled all the firstborn of the Israelites, as the Lord had commanded him.
The total number of firstborn males among the Israelites, counted by name from one month old and older in their enrollment, was twenty-two thousand two hundred seventy-three.
And the Lord spoke to Moses and said:
“Take the Levites in place of all the firstborn of the Israelites, and the livestock of the Levites in place of their livestock. The Levites shall belong to me, for I am the Lord.
As the ransom for the two hundred seventy-three firstborn of the Israelites who exceed the number of the Levites,
take five shekels per person, using the sanctuary double-drachma, at twenty gerahs to a shekel.
Give the silver to Aaron and his sons as the ransom for those who exceed their number.”
Moses took the redemption money from those who exceeded the number redeemed by the Levites.
From the firstborn of the Israelites, he took the silver: one thousand three hundred sixty-five shekels, according to the sanctuary shekel.
Moses gave the redemption money from those who exceeded that number to Aaron and his sons, according to the word of the Lord, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
The Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron and said:
Count the sons of Kohath from among the sons of Levi, according to their divisions and their ancestral houses.
From twenty-five years old and upward to fifty years old, everyone who enters service to perform any work in the tent of testimony.
This shall be the work of the sons of Kohath among the sons of Levi, according to their divisions and their ancestral households, in the tent of testimony: the most holy things.
Aaron and his sons shall enter when the camp sets out, take down the screening curtain, and cover the ark of testimony with it.
They shall put a blue leather covering over it, spread an entirely blue cloth over it on top, and insert its carrying poles.

Over the table of the Presence they shall spread a cloth entirely of purple, and place on it the plates, containers, cups, and vessels with which they pour offerings. The bread that is always there shall remain on it.
They shall spread a scarlet cloth over it, cover it with a blue leather covering, and insert its carrying poles.
They shall take a blue cloth and cover the lampstand for lighting, both its lamp holders, its tongs, its trays, and all the oil vessels used in its service.
They shall put it and all its equipment into a blue leather covering and place it on the carrying poles.
They shall cover the gold altar with a blue cloth, put a blue leather covering over it, and insert its carrying poles.
They shall take all the equipment used for service in the sanctuary, put it in blue cloths, cover it with a blue leather covering, and place it on the carrying poles.
They shall put the covering over the altar and cover it with a cloth entirely of purple.

They shall put on it the utensils with which they minister at it: the censers, the meat forks, the basins, the covers, and all the utensils of the altar. They shall spread a blue leather covering over it and pass its carrying poles through it. They shall take a purple cloth and cover the basin and its bases, spread blue leather over it, and place it on the carrying poles.

Aaron and his sons shall finish covering the holy things and all the equipment of the sanctuary when the camp sets out. Then the sons of Kohath shall enter to carry them, but they must not touch the holy things, lest they die. These are the things the sons of Kohath shall carry from the tent of testimony.

Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, shall be in charge of the oil for lighting, the prepared incense, the regular offering, the anointing oil, and the equipment of the entire tabernacle, everything in it, and everything in the sanctuary and among all the holy things.
The Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron and said:
Do not let the division of Kohath be destroyed from among the Levites.
Do this for them so that they may live and not die when they approach the most holy things: Aaron and his sons shall enter and assign each of them his duty and his load.
They must not enter recklessly to look at the most holy things, lest they die.
And the Lord spoke to Moses and said:
Take a census of the sons of Gershon according to their ancestral households and their divisions.
From twenty-five years old and upward to fifty years old, you shall register everyone who enters service to perform the work of the tent of testimony.
This shall be the service of the division of Gershon in entering the tent and carrying loads.
He shall carry the curtains of the tabernacle, the tent of testimony, its coverings, the blue covering that lies over it on top, and the curtain of the tent of testimony,
and the curtain of the courtyard, whatever is over the tent of testimony, the ropes, and all the equipment used in their service.

They shall do as Aaron and his sons command. The service of the sons of Gershon shall be under their direction in all their service and all their work. You shall register them by name, along with everything they are to carry.
This shall be the service of the sons of Gershon in the tent of testimony, and their duties shall be under the direction of Ithamar, the son of Aaron the priest.
You shall take a census of the sons of Merari by their clans and their ancestral households.
You shall count them from twenty-five years old and upward to fifty years old, everyone who enters the service to do the work of the tent of testimony.

These shall be the loads entrusted to them to carry, according to all their work in the tent of testimony: the capitals of the tent, its bars, its pillars, its bases, the curtain, their bases and their pillars, and the curtain at the entrance of the tent,

and the pillars around the courtyard and their bases, the pillars of the curtain at the entrance of the courtyard and their bases, their pegs, their cords, all their equipment, and everything used in their service. You shall register them by name, along with all the equipment entrusted to them to carry.
This shall be the service of the clan of the sons of Merari in all their work in the tent of testimony, under the direction of Ithamar, the son of Aaron the priest.
Moses, Aaron, and the leaders of Israel took a census of the sons of Kohath by their clans and their ancestral households,
from twenty-five years old and upward to fifty years old, everyone who entered the service and did work in the tent of testimony.
The number of them counted by their clans was two thousand seven hundred and fifty.
This is the census of the clan of Kohath, everyone who entered the service in the tent of testimony, whom Moses and Aaron counted at the command of the Lord through Moses.
The sons of Gershon were counted by their clans and their ancestral households,
from twenty-five years old and upward to fifty years old, everyone who entered to serve and do work in the tent of testimony.
The number of them counted by their clans and their ancestral households was two thousand six hundred and thirty.
This is the census of the clan of the sons of Gershon, everyone who served in the tent of testimony, whom Moses and Aaron counted according to the command of the Lord through Moses.
The clans of the sons of Merari were also counted by their clans and their ancestral households,
from twenty-five years old and upward to fifty years old, everyone who entered to serve in the work of the tent of testimony.
The number of them counted by their clans and their ancestral households was three thousand two hundred.
This is the census of the clan of the sons of Merari, whom Moses and Aaron counted according to the command of the Lord through Moses.
All the Levites who were counted, whom Moses, Aaron, and the leaders of Israel counted by their clans and their ancestral households.
From twenty-five years old and over, up to fifty years old: everyone who entered into the work of the holy things and the work of carrying the tabernacle of testimony.
Those included in the census were eight thousand five hundred eighty, according to the word of the Lord.
The Lord counted them through Moses, each man according to his work and the loads he carried. They were counted as the Lord commanded Moses.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said:
Command the sons of Israel to send out of the camp everyone with leprosy, everyone with a seminal discharge, and everyone made unclean by a dead person.
You shall send them out of the camp, male and female alike, so that they do not defile their camps, where I dwell.
The sons of Israel did so and sent them out of the camp. Just as the Lord spoke to Moses, so the sons of Israel did.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said:
Speak to the sons of Israel and say: If a man or woman commits any of the sins that people commit and acts with utter contempt, that person becomes guilty.
He shall confess the sins he has committed and repay the full amount for his offense, adding a fifth of it, and give it to the person he has wronged.

But if the man has no close relative to whom restitution for the offense can be made, the restitution offered to the Lord shall belong to the priest, besides the ram of atonement with which atonement is made for him.
Every offering from all the things consecrated by the Israelites, whatever they present to the Lord, shall belong to the priest.
Each person's consecrated things shall belong to him, and whatever anyone gives to the priest shall belong to the priest.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said:
Speak to the Israelites and say to them: If any man's wife goes astray and treats him with contempt,

And someone lies with her, with an emission of semen, and it escapes her husband's notice, and she conceals it, though she has been defiled, and there is no witness against her, and she is not pregnant,

and a spirit of jealousy comes upon her husband and he becomes jealous of his wife, though she has been defiled; or a spirit of jealousy comes upon him and he becomes jealous of his wife, though she has not been defiled,

the man shall bring his wife to the priest and present an offering on her behalf: a tenth of an ephah of barley flour. He shall pour no oil on it and put no frankincense on it, for it is an offering of jealousy, a memorial offering, an offering that brings sins to remembrance.
The priest shall bring the woman forward and set her before the Lord.
The priest shall take holy, fresh water in an earthenware vessel, and the priest shall take some of the dust from the floor of the tent of testimony and put it into the water.

The priest shall set the woman before the Lord, uncover the woman's head, and place in her hands the memorial offering, the offering of jealousy. In the priest's hand shall be the water of testing that brings the curse.

The priest shall put her under oath and say to the woman, “If no man has lain with you, and if you have not gone astray and become defiled while married to your husband, may you be free from this water of testing that brings the curse.
But if you have gone astray while married to your husband, or have been defiled, and someone other than your husband has had sexual intercourse with you—”

then the priest shall put the woman under oath with this oath of cursing, and the priest shall say to the woman, “May the Lord make you a curse and an oath among your people, when the Lord makes your thighs waste away and your belly swell.
May this cursed water enter your belly, making your abdomen swell and your thighs waste away.” And the woman shall say, “So be it, so be it.”
The priest shall write these curses in a scroll and wash them off into the water of testing that brings the curses.
He shall give the woman the water of testing that brings the curses to drink, and the cursed water of testing shall enter her.
The priest shall take the offering of jealousy from the woman's hands, place the offering before the Lord, and bring it to the altar.
The priest shall take a handful from the offering as its memorial portion and offer it on the altar. Afterward he shall give the woman the water of testing to drink.

If she has been defiled and has kept it completely hidden from her husband, the cursed water of testing shall enter her, her belly shall swell, and her thighs shall waste away. The woman shall become a curse among her people.
But if the woman has not been defiled and is pure, she shall be free from guilt and shall conceive.
This shall be the law of jealousy when a married woman has gone astray and become defiled,
or when a spirit of jealousy comes upon a man and he becomes jealous of his wife. He shall set the woman before the Lord, and the priest shall do to her everything prescribed in this law.
The man shall be free from sin, and the woman shall bear her own sins.
And the Lord spoke to Moses and said:
Speak to the Israelites and say: “If a man or woman makes a solemn vow to consecrate himself or herself to the Lord,”
He shall abstain from wine and strong drink. He shall drink neither wine vinegar nor strong-drink vinegar, and he shall eat neither its grapes nor raisins.
Throughout all the days of his vow, he shall eat nothing that comes from the grapevine, from raisins to grape seeds.
Throughout all the days of his consecration, no razor shall pass over his head. Until the days that he vowed to the Lord are fulfilled, he shall remain holy, letting the hair of his head grow long.
Throughout all the days of his vow to the Lord, he shall not go near a dead person.
He shall not defile himself for his father, his mother, his brother, or his sister when they die, because the vow to the Lord is upon his head.
Throughout all the days of his vow, he shall remain holy to the Lord.
If someone suddenly dies beside him, his consecrated head will immediately be defiled. He shall shave his head on the day he is purified; on the seventh day he shall shave it.
On the eighth day he shall bring two turtledoves or two young pigeons to the priest at the entrance of the tabernacle of testimony.

The priest shall offer one as a sin offering and one as a burnt offering. The priest shall make atonement for him for the sin he committed concerning a person, and he shall consecrate his head on that day.
For on that day he consecrated the days of his vow to the Lord. He shall bring a year-old lamb as a guilt offering, and the former days shall not be counted, because his consecrated head was defiled.
This shall be the law for the Nazirite: on the day when he completes the days of his vow, he shall be brought to the entrance of the tabernacle of testimony.
He shall present his offering to the Lord: one unblemished year-old male lamb as a burnt offering, one unblemished year-old ewe lamb as a sin offering, and one unblemished ram as a peace offering.
He shall also bring a basket of unleavened bread made from fine flour, cakes mixed with oil, and unleavened wafers spread with oil, together with their grain offerings and their drink offerings.
The priest shall present them before the Lord and offer his sin offering and his burnt offering.
He shall offer the ram as a peace offering to the Lord, together with the basket of unleavened bread, and the priest shall offer its grain offering and its drink offerings.
The Nazirite shall shave his consecrated head at the entrance of the tabernacle of testimony and place the hair in the fire beneath the peace offering.

The priest shall take the boiled shoulder from the ram, one unleavened cake from the basket, and one unleavened wafer. After the Nazirite has shaved his head, the priest shall place them in his hands.

The priest shall present these as an offering before the Lord. They shall be holy and belong to the priest, in addition to the breast presented as an offering and the shoulder set aside as a contribution. Afterward the Nazirite may drink wine.

This shall be the law for a Nazirite who vows his offering to the Lord for his vow, apart from whatever else he can afford, according to the extent of the vow he makes, in accordance with the law of consecration to the Lord.
And the Lord spoke to Moses and said:
He spoke to Aaron and his sons, and you shall say: “This is how you shall bless the Israelites; say to them:
May the Lord bless you and keep you.
May the Lord show his face to you and have mercy on you.
May the Lord lift up his face toward you and give you peace.
They shall place my name upon the Israelites, and I will bless them.
It happened on the day when Moses finished setting up the tabernacle and anointed it and all its furnishings, and the altar and all its furnishings. He anointed them and consecrated them.
And the leaders of Israel brought offerings: the twelve leaders of their ancestral houses. They were the leaders of the tribes, and they were in charge of the census.
They presented their gifts before the Lord: six decorated wagons and twelve oxen, one wagon from every two leaders and one ox from each leader. They brought them before the tabernacle.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said:
Take these from them, and let them be used for the service of the tabernacle of testimony. Give them to the Levites, to each according to his service.
And Moses took the carts and the oxen and gave them to the Levites.
He gave two carts and four oxen to the sons of Gershon, according to their service.
And he gave four carts and eight oxen to the sons of Merari, according to their service, under the direction of Ithamar, the son of Aaron the priest.
But he gave nothing to the sons of Kohath, because they were responsible for the service of the Holy of Holies and carried its objects on their shoulders.
And the leaders presented offerings for the dedication of the altar on the day when it was anointed, and the leaders brought their offerings before the altar.
And the Lord said to Moses, “Let the leaders present their offerings for the dedication of the altar, one leader each day.”
And on the first day Nahshon son of Amminadab, leader of the tribe of Judah, presented his offering.

He presented his offering: one silver basin weighing 130 units of weight, one silver bowl weighing seventy shekels according to the sanctuary shekel, both filled with fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering;
one gold incense vessel weighing ten darics, filled with incense;
one young bull from the herd, one ram, and one year-old lamb for a burnt offering;
And one male goat as a sin offering.

His offerings: one silver basin weighing one hundred thirty units, one silver bowl weighing seventy shekels according to the sanctuary shekel, both filled with fine flour mixed with oil as a grain offering.

His offerings: one silver basin weighing one hundred thirty units, one silver bowl weighing seventy shekels according to the sanctuary shekel, both filled with fine flour mixed with oil as a grain offering.

This is the rite for the dedication of the altar on the day when it was anointed, from the leaders of the Israelites: twelve silver basins, twelve silver bowls, and twelve boxes.

One basin weighing one hundred and thirty shekels and one bowl weighing seventy shekels. All the silver of the vessels amounted to two thousand four hundred shekels, according to the sanctuary shekel.
Twelve gold incense bowls, filled with incense. All the gold of the bowls amounted to one hundred and twenty gold pieces.

And all the cattle for the burnt offering were twelve young bulls, twelve rams, and twelve unblemished year-old lambs, with their grain offerings and their drink offerings, and twelve male goats for sin offerings.

And all the cattle for the burnt-offering sacrifice were twelve; there were twenty-four heifers, sixty rams, sixty male goats, and sixty unblemished year-old ewe lambs. These were the dedication offerings for the altar after their hands had been consecrated.

When Moses entered the tent of testimony to speak with him, he heard the voice of the Lord speaking with him from above the mercy seat, from between the two cherubim that were over the ark of testimony, from between the two cherubim; and he spoke with him.
And the Lord spoke to Moses and said:
Speak to Aaron and say to him: When you set up the lamps, all seven lamps shall burn on one side, in front of the lampstand.
And Aaron did so: he lit its lamps on one side, facing the lampstand, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
And this was the construction of the lampstand: cast gold, its stem and its lilies all cast together. He made the lampstand according to the pattern that the Lord had shown Moses.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said:
Take the Levites from among the Israelites and purify them.
And this is how you shall purify them: sprinkle them with water of purification, let a razor pass over their entire bodies, and let them wash their clothes and become clean.
And they shall take one young bull from the herd, with its grain offering of fine flour mixed with oil; and you shall take a year-old calf from the herd for a sin offering.
And you shall bring the Levites before the tent of testimony and gather the whole congregation of the descendants of Israel.
And they shall present the Levites before the Lord, and the descendants of Israel shall lay their hands on the Levites.
And Aaron shall set the Levites apart from the descendants of Israel as an offering before the Lord, and they shall perform the work of the tent before the Lord.
And the Levites shall lay their hands on the heads of the young bulls, and you shall offer one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering to the Lord, to make atonement for them.
And you shall place the Levites before the Lord, before Aaron, and before his sons, and give them as an offering before the Lord.
And you shall set the Levites apart from among the descendants of Israel, and they shall be mine.
And afterward the Levites shall enter to perform the work of the tent of testimony. You shall purify them and give them as an offering before the Lord.
For they have been given to me as a gift from among the Israelites. In place of all the firstborn who open every womb among the Israelites, I have taken them for myself.
For every firstborn among the Israelites is mine, both human and animal. On the day when I struck down every firstborn in the land of Egypt, I consecrated them to myself.
And I took the Levites in place of all the firstborn sons of Israel.

And I gave the Levites as a gift to Aaron and his sons from among the Israelites, to perform the work of the Israelites in the tent of testimony and to make atonement for the Israelites when they approach the holy things.
Moses, Aaron, and the whole congregation of the Israelites did for the Levites as the Lord commanded Moses concerning the Levites. So the Israelites did for them.
The Levites purified themselves and washed their clothes, and they gave themselves to Aaron as a gift before the Lord. Aaron made atonement for them to purify them.
Afterward the Levites entered to perform their service in the tent of testimony before Aaron and his sons. As the Lord commanded Moses concerning the Levites, so they did for them.
And the Lord spoke to Moses and said:
This is what applies to the Levites: from twenty-five years old and upward, they shall enter to work in the tent of testimony.
From fifty years old, they shall withdraw from that service and shall no longer work.
His brother shall serve in the tent of testimony and shall keep its duties, but he shall do no work. This is how you shall deal with the Levites regarding their duties.
The Lord spoke to Moses in the wilderness of Sinai, in the second year after they came out of Egypt, in the first month, and said:
Tell the Israelites to observe the Passover at its appointed time.
On the fourteenth day of the first month, they shall observe it at evening, at the appointed time. They shall observe it according to its law and its regulations.
Moses spoke to the Israelites about observing the Passover.
At the beginning of the fourteenth day of the month, in the wilderness of Sinai, the Israelites did as the Lord commanded Moses.
There were men who were unclean because of a human corpse and could not celebrate the Passover on that day. They came before Moses and Aaron on that day.
Those men said to them, “We are unclean because of a human corpse. Now let us not be [?] from presenting the Lord’s offering at its appointed time among the Israelites.”
Moses said to them, “Stay there, and I will hear what instructions the Lord gives concerning you.”
And the Lord spoke to Moses and said:
Speak to the Israelites and say: If anyone among you or your descendants is unclean because of a human corpse, or is on a distant journey, he shall observe the Passover to the Lord.
In the second month, on the fourteenth day, at evening, he shall observe it. They shall eat it with unleavened bread and [?].
They shall leave none of it until morning and shall break no bone of it. They shall observe it according to the law of the Passover.

But anyone who is clean and is not on a distant journey, yet neglects to observe the Passover, shall be cut off from his people, because he did not present the Lord’s offering at its appointed time. That man shall bear his sin.

If a foreigner joins you in your land and observes the Passover to the Lord, he shall observe it according to the rule of the Passover and its regulations. You shall have one and the same law for the foreigner and the native of the land.
On the day when the tent was set up, the cloud covered the tent and the house of testimony. In the evening, something like the appearance of fire was over the tent until morning.
It was always so: a cloud covered it by day, and the appearance of fire by night.
Whenever the cloud rose from the tent, the Israelites would set out. In the place where the cloud settled, there the Israelites would camp.
At the Lord’s command the Israelites set out, and at the Lord’s command they encamped. Throughout all the days when the cloud covers the tabernacle, the Israelites shall remain encamped.
When the cloud remains over the tabernacle for many days, the Israelites shall keep the Lord’s charge and shall not set out.
When the cloud covers the tabernacle for a few days, they shall encamp at the Lord’s word, and at the Lord’s word they shall set out.
When the cloud remains from evening until morning, if the cloud rises in the morning, they shall set out, whether by day or by night. But if the cloud does not rise, they shall not set out.
If the cloud lingers for a month and overshadows it, the Israelites shall remain encamped and shall not set out.
At the Lord’s command they shall set out, and they shall keep the Lord’s charge, according to the Lord’s command through Moses.
And the Lord spoke to Moses and said:
Make yourself two silver trumpets; you shall make them of hammered silver. They shall serve you for summoning the people and for setting the camps in motion.
They shall sound the trumpets, and all the people shall gather at the entrance of the tabernacle of testimony.
If they sound only one trumpet, the leaders, the commanders of Israel, shall come to you.
You shall sound a trumpet alarm, and the camps encamped on the east shall set out.

You shall sound the second trumpet alarm, and the camps encamped on the south shall set out. You shall sound the third trumpet alarm, and the camps encamped on the west shall set out. You shall sound the fourth trumpet alarm, and the camps encamped on the north shall set out. They shall sound a trumpet alarm when they set out.
When you gather the people, you shall sound the trumpet, but not an alarm.
The sons of Aaron, the priests, shall sound the trumpets. This shall be a perpetual statute for you throughout your generations.
If you go to war in your land against adversaries who oppose you, you shall sound an alarm with the trumpet. You shall be remembered before the Lord and shall be saved from your enemies.

On your days of rejoicing and at your new moons, you shall sound the trumpets over your burnt offerings and over your sacrifices of peace offerings. They shall serve as a memorial for you before your God. I am the Lord your God.
In the second year, in the second month, on the twentieth day of the month, the cloud rose from the tabernacle of testimony.
And the Israelites set out with their households from the wilderness of Sinai, and the cloud rested in the wilderness of Paran.
The Israelites set out at the Lord’s word through Moses.
The divisions of the camp of the descendants of Judah set out first, at the head, with their forces. Nahshon son of Amminadab was over their forces.
Nethanel son of Zuar was over the forces of the descendants of Issachar.
Eliab son of Helon was over the forces of the tribe of the descendants of Zebulun.
They took down the tabernacle, and the sons of Gershon and the sons of Merari set out, carrying the tabernacle.
The divisions of the camp of the descendants of Reuben set out with their forces. Elizur son of Shedeur was over their forces.
Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai was over the forces of the tribe of the descendants of Simeon.
Elizaphan son of Deuel was over the forces of the tribe of the descendants of Gad.
The sons of Kohath shall set out, carrying the holy things, and they shall set up the tabernacle before the others arrive.
The divisions of the camp of Ephraim set out with their forces. Elishama son of Ammihud was over their forces.
Gamaliel son of Pedahzur was over the forces of the tribe of the descendants of Manasseh.
And over the army of the tribe of Benjamin was Abidan son of Gideoni.
The divisions of the camp of the descendants of Dan set out after all the other camps, with their forces. Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai was over their forces.
And over the army of the tribe of the sons of Asher was Pagiel son of Ocran.
And over the army of the tribe of the sons of Naphtali was Ahira son of Enan.
These are the armies of the sons of Israel, and they set out with their armies.

And Moses said to Hobab son of Reuel the Midianite, Moses’ father-in-law, “Look, we are setting out for the place that the Lord said he would give us. Come with us, and we will treat you well, for the Lord has promised good things to Israel.”
And he said, “I will not go there, but I will go to my own land and my own people.”
And he said to him, “Do not leave us, for you were with us in the wilderness, and you shall be an elder among us.”
“And if you go with us, whatever good things the Lord does for us, we will also do for you.”
And they set out from the mountain of the Lord on a three-day journey, and the ark of the covenant of the Lord went ahead of them on the three-day journey to find a resting place for them.
And the cloud sheltered them by day when they set out from the camp.
And whenever the ark set out, Moses said, “Rise, Lord, and let your enemies be scattered; let all who hate you flee.”
And when it came to rest, he said, “Return, Lord, to the thousands and tens of thousands of Israel.”
And the people grumbled bitterly before the Lord, and the Lord heard and became furious. Fire from the Lord blazed among them and consumed part of the camp.
And the people cried out to Moses, and Moses prayed to the Lord, and the fire stopped.
And that place was named Taberah, because fire from the Lord blazed among them.
And the mixed multitude among them had a craving, and the Israelites sat down and wept, saying, “Who will give us meat to eat?”
“For we remembered the fish that we ate in Egypt for nothing, and the cucumbers, melons, leeks, onions, and garlic.
And now we are wasting away, and our eyes see nothing anywhere except manna.”
And the manna was like white coriander seed, and its appearance was like the appearance of ice.
And the people went about gathering it, grinding it in a mill or pounding it in a mortar. They cooked it in a pot and made cakes from it, and its sweetness was like a cake made with oil and honey.
And when the dew descended on the camp at night, the manna also descended upon it.
Moses heard them weeping in their groups, each at the entrance of his own tent. The Lord became exceedingly angry, and it seemed evil to Moses.
And Moses said to the Lord, “Why, Lord, have you afflicted your servant? And why have I not found favor before you, that you have laid the anger of these people upon me?
Did I conceive all these people, or did I give birth to them, that you say to me, ‘Carry them in your bosom, as a nurse carries a nursing child, to the land that you swore to their fathers’?
And now, where am I to get meat to give all these people? For they weep at me and say, ‘Give us meat to eat.’
I cannot carry these people alone, for this task is too heavy for me.
If you are going to treat me this way, kill me outright, if it pleases you, if I have found favor and mercy from you, so that I may not see my suffering.”

And the Lord said to Moses, “Gather for me seventy men from the elders of Israel, whom you know to be elders of the people and their chosen men. Bring them to the tent of testimony, and let them stand there with you.

And I will come down there and speak with you. I will take some of the Spirit that is upon you and put it upon them, and they will bear the insolence of these people with you, so that you will not bear them alone.

And you shall say to the people, ‘Consecrate yourselves for tomorrow, and you will eat meat, for you have wept before the Lord and said, “Who will give us meat? For we were better off in Egypt.” And the Lord will give you meat to eat, and you will eat meat.’
You shall not eat for one day, or two days, or five days, or ten days, or twenty days.

Rather, you shall eat for a whole month, until it comes out through your nostrils and becomes bitter to you, because you rebelled against the Lord who is among you, and you wept before him and said, ‘Why did we leave Egypt?’
Moses said, “The people among whom I am number six hundred thousand men on foot, yet you say, ‘I will give them meat, and they will eat for a whole month.’
“Can cattle and sheep be slaughtered in sufficient numbers for them? Or can all the fish of the sea be gathered to provide enough for them?”
The Lord said to Moses, “Is the Lord’s hand not sufficient? Now you will know whether my word will come true for you or not.”
Moses went out and told the people the Lord’s words. He gathered seventy men from among the elders of the people and stationed them around the tent.

The Lord came down in a cloud and spoke with Moses. He took some of the Spirit that was upon him and placed it upon the seventy elders. When the Spirit rested upon them, they prophesied in the camp, but did not do so again.

Two men remained in the camp. One was named Eldad, and the other Medad. The Spirit rested upon them. They were among those whose names had been recorded, but they had not come to the tent, and they prophesied in the camp.
A young man ran and reported to Moses, saying to him, “Eldad and Medad are prophesying in the camp.”
Joshua son of Nun, Moses’ chosen attendant, responded and said, “My lord Moses, stop them!”
Moses said to him, “Do not be jealous on my behalf! If only all the Lord’s people were prophets, and the Lord would put his Spirit upon them!”
Moses returned to the camp, together with the elders of Israel.

A wind came from the Lord and brought quail over from the sea. They fell around the camp, a day’s journey on this side and a day’s journey on that side, all around the camp, about two cubits above the ground.

The people rose and gathered the quail all that day, all that night, and all the next day. Whoever gathered the least gathered ten cors. They slaughtered them and smoked the meat for themselves in batches all around the camp.
While the meat was still between their teeth, before it ran out, the Lord became angry with the people, and the Lord struck the people with very great plagues.
That place was named Graves of Craving, because there they buried the people who had craved the meat.
From Graves of Craving the people set out for Hazeroth.
Miriam and Aaron spoke against Moses because of the Ethiopian woman whom Moses had married, for he had married an Ethiopian woman.
They said, “Has the Lord spoken only with Moses? Has he not also spoken with us?” And the Lord heard.
Now the man Moses was very humble, more than all the people on the earth.
The Lord immediately said to Moses, Aaron, and Miriam, “Come out, all three of you, to the tent of testimony.” And all three came out to the tent of testimony.
The Lord came down in a pillar of cloud and stood at the entrance of the tent of testimony. Aaron and Miriam were called, and both came forward.
The Lord said to them, “Listen to my words. If there is a prophet of the Lord among you, I will appear to him in a vision and speak with him in a dream.
“It is not so with my servant Moses, who is faithful in all my house.
“I will speak with him mouth to mouth, visibly and not in riddles, and he has seen the glory of the Lord. Why, then, were you not afraid to speak against my servant Moses?”
The Lord’s fierce anger came upon them, and they departed.
And the cloud rose from the tent, and there was Miriam, leprous, white as snow. Aaron looked at Miriam, and there she was, leprous.
And Aaron said to Moses, “I beg you, my lord, do not lay sin upon us, for we acted ignorantly and sinned.”
Let her not be like the dead, like a miscarried child that comes out of its mother's womb and consumes half her flesh.
And Moses cried out to the Lord and said, "I beg you, God, heal her."
And the Lord said to Moses, "If her father had spat in her face, would she not be ashamed for seven days? Let her be separated outside the camp for seven days, and then let her come in."
And Miriam was separated outside the camp for seven days, and the people did not set out until Miriam was cleansed.
And afterward the people set out from Hazeroth and camped in the wilderness of Paran.
And the Lord spoke to Moses and said:

Send men to spy out the land of the Canaanites, which I will give to the children of Israel as a possession. You shall send one man from each tribe, according to their ancestral households, all of them leaders among their people.
And Moses sent them from the wilderness of Paran according to the word of the Lord. They were all men who were leaders among the children of Israel.
And these are their names: from the tribe of Reuben, Salamiel son of Zaccur.
From the tribe of Simeon, Shaphat son of Hori.
From the tribe of Judah, Caleb son of Jephunneh.
From the tribe of Issachar, Igal son of Joseph.
From the tribe of Ephraim, Hoshea son of Nun.
From the tribe of Benjamin, Palti son of Raphu.
From the tribe of Zebulun, Judiel son of Sodi.
From the tribe of Joseph, from the children of Manasseh, Gaddi son of Susi.
From the tribe of Dan, Ammiel son of Gama.
From the tribe of Asher, Sethur son of Michael.
From the tribe of Naphtali, Abi son of Jabiah.
From the tribe of Gad, Geuel son of Machi.
These are the names of the men whom the Lord sent to spy out the land of the Canaanites. And Moses gave Hoshea son of Nun the name Joshua.
And Moses sent them from the wilderness of Paran to spy out the land of the Canaanites, and said to them, "Go up through this wilderness and climb into the hill country,
and see what the land is like, and whether the people who live in it are strong or weak, few or many,
and what the land in which they live is like, whether it is good or bad, and what the cities in which they live are like, whether they are walled or unwalled,

and what the land is like, whether it is fertile or poor, and whether there are trees in it or not. Be courageous and take some of the fruit of the land." It was springtime, the days of the first ripe grapes.
And they went up and spied out the land from the wilderness of Sinai as far as Rehob, at the entrance to Ephrath.
They went up through the wilderness and came as far as Hebron. Ahiman, Sheshai, and Talmai, descendants of Anak, were there. Hebron had been built seven years before Tanis in Egypt.

They came as far as the Valley of the Cluster and explored it. From there they cut a vine branch with a single cluster of grapes on it, and they carried it on poles, along with some pomegranates and figs.
They named the place the Valley of the Cluster because of the cluster that the Israelites cut from there.
After forty days, the Israelites returned from exploring the land.
They came to Moses, Aaron, and the whole assembly of the Israelites at Kadesh in the wilderness of Paran. They gave them and the whole assembly their report and showed them the fruit of the land.
They reported to him and said, “We went to the land to which you sent us, a land flowing with milk and honey, and this is its fruit.
But the people living in it were powerful, and the cities were fortified, walled, and very large. We also saw the descendants of Anak there.
The Amalekites live in the southern part of the land. The Hittites, Hivites, Jebusites, and Amorites live in the mountains, and the Canaanites live along the seacoast and beside the Jordan.”
Caleb quieted the people before Moses and said to them, “It is not so! Let us go up and take possession of it, for we are able to defeat them.”
And the men who had gone with him said, “Let us not go up, for we cannot go against the nation, because it is much stronger than we are.”

And they frightened the Israelites about the land they had explored, saying, “The land through which we passed to explore it is a land that devours its inhabitants, and all the people we saw in it are men of great stature.”
“We also saw giants there, and in their eyes we were like grasshoppers.”
The whole assembly raised their voices, and the people wept all that night.
All the Israelites grumbled against Moses and Aaron, and the whole assembly said to them, “It would have been better if we had died in Egypt, or if we had died right here in this wilderness!
Why is the Lord bringing us into that land to fall in battle? Our wives and our children will be taken as plunder. Now it would be better for us to return to Egypt.”
And each man said to his companion, “Let us appoint a leader and return to Egypt.”
Moses and Aaron fell on their faces before the whole assembly of the Israelites.
But Joshua son of Nun and Caleb son of Jephunneh, who were among those who had explored the land, tore their clothes.
They spoke to the whole assembly of the Israelites and said, “The land that we explored is a very good land.
If only the Lord is pleased with us, he will bring us into that land and give it to us—a land flowing with milk and honey.”
Only do not rebel against the Lord, and do not fear the people of the land, for they are food for us. The Lord has departed from them, and the Lord is with us. Do not be afraid of them.”
And all the people said to stone them with stones, and the glory of the Lord appeared in a cloud over the tent of testimony before all the Israelites.
The Lord said to Moses, “How long will this people provoke me to anger? How long will they refuse to believe in me, despite all the signs I have performed among them?
Let me strike them with death and destroy them, and I will make you and your father’s household into a nation greater and more numerous than this one.”
Moses said to the Lord, “Now the Egyptians will hear that you brought this people out from among them by your great power.

All the inhabitants of this land will also hear that you, Lord, are among this people, that you, Lord, appear face to face, that your cloud stands over them, and that you go before them in a pillar of cloud by day and a pillar of fire by night.
If you destroy this people of yours as though they were one man, the nations that have heard of your name will say,
‘Because the Lord could not bring that people into the land he had sworn to give them, he struck them down in that wilderness.’
Now let your hand be exalted, Lord, just as you spoke and said,

‘The Lord is patient, abundant in mercy, and true. He takes away lawlessness, wrongdoing, and sins, but he does not acquit the guilty. He punishes the children for the sins of their fathers to the third and fourth generations.’
Forgive the sins of your people according to your great mercy, as you have forgiven them from Egypt until now.
And the Lord said to Moses, “I will forgive them according to your word.
But as I live, and as my name lives, the glory of the Lord shall fill the whole earth.
For all the men who saw my glory and the signs that I performed in Egypt and in this wilderness, and who tested me these ten times and did not listen to my voice,

shall certainly not see the land that I swore to give their fathers. But their children who are here with me, who do not know evil or good—to all their little ones who lack understanding I will give the land. And none of those who provoked me to anger shall see it.
But my servant Caleb, in whom there was a different spirit and who followed me, I will bring into the land he entered, and his descendants shall inherit it.
The Amalekites and the Canaanites live in the valley. But tomorrow you must turn back and set out into the wilderness by the road to the Red Sea.”
The Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron and said:
“How long shall I put up with this evil people? They grumble before me. I have heard the complaints of the children of Israel, who grumble against you.
Now say to them, ‘As I live, says the Lord, I will certainly do to you just as you have spoken in my hearing.
Your bones shall fall in this wilderness, along with your entire company—all of you who were counted, from twenty years old and upward, who grumbled against me.
You shall certainly not enter the land in which I raised my hand and swore to settle you, except Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun.
But your children, whom you said would become plunder, I will bring into the land, and they shall inherit the land that you despised.
Your bones shall fall here in this wilderness.
Your children shall live as shepherds here in the wilderness for forty years and bear the burden of your unfaithfulness until your bones waste away here in the wilderness.
According to the number of the forty days, a day for a year, you shall bear your sins for forty years, and you shall know the fury of my anger.
I, the Lord, have spoken. I will certainly do this to this evil people who have risen against me. Here in the wilderness they shall perish, and here they shall die.’”
And the men whom Moses sent to spy out the land returned and spoke against it to the people, spreading a bad report about the land.
Those men who spread a bad report about the land died from grievous blows before the Lord.
Only Joshua son of Nun and Caleb son of Jephunneh survived from among those men who had gone to spy out the land.
And Moses spoke these words to all the children of Israel, and the people mourned deeply.
They rose early in the morning and went up to the top of the mountain, saying, “Here we are. We will go up to the place that the Lord spoke of, for we have sinned.”
And Moses said, “Why do you transgress the word of the Lord? You will not succeed.
Do not go up, for the Lord is not with you, and you will fall before your enemies.
For the Amalekites and the Canaanites are there before you, and you will fall by the sword. Because you turned back and rebelled against the Lord, the Lord will not be with you.”
But they disobeyed and went up to the top of the mountain. The ark of the Lord’s covenants and Moses, however, did not move from the camp.
The Amalekites and the Canaanites who lived on the mountain came down, struck them, and slaughtered them as far as Hormah.
And they returned to the camp.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said:
Speak to the Israelites and say to them: When you enter the land where you will live, which I will give you,

And you shall make a burnt offering to the Lord and a whole offering as a sacrifice, to fulfill a vow or as a freewill offering or at your festivals, to make a pleasing aroma for the Lord, whether from cattle or from the flocks.
the one who presents his offering to the Lord shall bring a grain offering of a tenth of an ephah of fine flour mixed with a quarter of a hin of oil.
And you shall prepare a quarter of a hin of wine as a drink offering with the sacrifice or burnt offering, for each lamb. This much you shall prepare as an offering of a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
And when you prepare a ram as a burnt offering or sacrifice, you shall prepare a grain offering of two-tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with a third of a hin of oil.
And you shall present half a hin of wine as a drink offering, as a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
But if you prepare an animal from the herd as a burnt offering or sacrifice, to fulfill vows or as a peace offering to the Lord,
you shall present with the bull a grain offering of three-tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with half a hin of oil,
and half a hin of wine as a drink offering, an offering of a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
You shall do this for each bull, each ram, or each lamb from the sheep or goats.
According to the number of animals you prepare, you shall do the same for each one, according to their individual number.
Every native shall do the same when presenting such offerings of a pleasing aroma to the Lord.

And if a foreigner settles among you in your land, whoever is among you throughout your generations, he shall make an offering of a pleasing aroma to the Lord. As you do, so shall the foreigner and the Lord’s congregation do.
One and the same law shall apply to you and to the foreigners who settle among you, an everlasting law throughout your generations. As you are, so shall the foreigner be before the Lord.
One and the same law shall apply, and one and the same rule shall be for you and for the foreigner who lives among you.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said:
Speak to the Israelites and say to them: When you enter the land into which I will bring you,
when you eat the bread of the land,

you shall set apart a contribution as an offering to the Lord from the first of your dough, and you shall bring the loaf of the contribution to the Lord. You shall set it apart for the Lord; as you set apart a contribution from the threshing floor, so shall you set this apart.
From the first of your dough you shall give a contribution to the Lord throughout your generations.
But when you transgress and do not carry out all these commandments that the Lord spoke to Moses,
as the Lord commanded you through Moses, from the day when the Lord commanded you and onward throughout your generations,

if something is done unintentionally without the congregation’s knowledge, the congregation shall prepare one unblemished bull from the herd as a burnt offering of a pleasing aroma to the Lord, with its grain offering and its drink offering according to the prescribed requirement, and one male goat as a sin offering.

And the priest shall make atonement for the whole congregation of the Israelites, and they shall be forgiven, because it was unintentional. They shall present their offering, a gift to the Lord for their sins, before the Lord, on account of their unintentional wrongdoing.
And the whole congregation of the Israelites and the foreigner who lives among you shall be forgiven, because the unintentional wrongdoing belongs to the whole congregation.
And if one person sins unintentionally, that person shall present a year-old female goat as a sin offering.
And the priest shall make atonement before the Lord for the person who has acted unintentionally and sinned unintentionally, to make atonement for him.
For the native-born among the Israelites and the foreigner who has settled among them, one and the same law shall apply to anyone who acts unintentionally.
But the person who acts arrogantly, whether native-born or a foreigner, has provoked the Lord. That person shall be cut off from his people.
For he has rejected the word of the Lord and broken his commandments. That person shall be utterly removed from his people, for his sins remain upon him.
While the Israelites were there in the wilderness, they found a man gathering wood on the Sabbath day.
Those who found him gathering wood on the Sabbath day brought him to Moses and Aaron and to the whole congregation of the Israelites.
And they put him in custody, because they had not determined what they should do to him.
And the Lord spoke to Moses and said, “The man must be put to death. The whole congregation shall stone him outside the camp.”
And the whole congregation brought him outside the camp, and the whole congregation stoned him outside the camp, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said:
Speak to the Israelites and tell them to make tassels on the corners of their garments throughout their generations, and to put a blue cord on the tassels at the corners.

And it shall be on your tassels, so that you may see it and remember all the commandments of the Lord and carry them out, and not turn aside after your own thoughts and eyes, by following which you prostitute yourselves.
So that you may remember and carry out all my commandments and be holy to your God.
For I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of the Egyptians to be your God. I am the Lord your God.
And Korah son of Izhar, son of Kohath, son of Levi, spoke, along with Dathan and Abiram, sons of Eliab, son of Reuben, and On son of Peleth, son of Reuben.
And they stood against Moses, along with two hundred and fifty men from among the Israelites, leaders of the congregation, members of the council, and men of renown.

They gathered against Moses and Aaron and said, “Enough from you! The whole congregation, every one of them, is holy, and the Lord is among them. Why then do you exalt yourselves above the congregation of the Lord?”
When Moses heard this, he fell on his face.

And he spoke to Korah and all his company and said, “God has visited and recognized those who are his and the one who is holy, and has brought him near to himself; but those whom he did not choose he did not bring near to himself.”
“Now do this: take your censers, Korah and all his company,
and put fire in them and place incense in them before the Lord tomorrow. The man whom the Lord chooses shall be the holy one. Enough from you, sons of Levi!”
And Moses said to Korah, “Listen to me, sons of Levi.

Is it a small thing to you that the God of Israel has separated you from his people and brought you near to himself to perform the service of the Lord’s tabernacle and to stand before the congregation to serve it?
He has brought you near to himself, and all your brothers, the sons of Levi, with you. Do you seek the priesthood as well?
Thus you and your company have gathered against God. And who is Aaron that you grumble against him?”
And Moses sent to summon Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab, but they said, “We will not come.
Is it a small thing that you brought us out of a land flowing with milk and honey to kill us here in the wilderness? And now do you also lord it over us, and are you the ruler?”
Have you brought us into a land flowing with milk and honey and given us an inheritance of fields and vineyards there? Even if you gouge out our eyes, we will not come to you.
Moses became very angry and said to the Lord, “Do not look upon their offerings, for I have taken nothing desirable belonging to any of them, nor have I mistreated any of them.”
Moses said to Korah, “Sanctify your assembly, and be ready before the Lord tomorrow, you and Aaron.
Each of you must take his own censer, put incense in it, and present his own censer before the Lord—the two hundred and fifty censers. You and Aaron must each bring your own censer.”
They put fire in them and placed incense in them, and Moses and Aaron stood at the entrance of the tent of testimony.
Korah gathered his entire assembly against them at the entrance of the tent of testimony, and the glory of the Lord appeared to the whole assembly.
The Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron and said,
“Separate yourselves from this assembly, and I will destroy them all at once.”
They fell on their faces and said, “God, God of the spirits of all flesh, if one man has sinned, will the Lord’s anger come upon the whole assembly?”
And the Lord spoke to Moses and said:
“Speak to the assembly and say, ‘Withdraw from around the assembly of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram.’”
Moses rose and went to Dathan and Abiram, and all the elders of Israel went with him.
He spoke to the assembly and said, “Depart from the tents of these hardhearted men, and do not come near anything belonging to them, lest you perish in all their sins.”
They withdrew from around Korah’s assembly. Dathan and Abiram came out and stood at the entrances of their tents, along with their wives, their children, and their households.
Moses said, “By this you will know that the Lord sent me to do all these deeds, and that none of it comes from me:
If these men die as all people die, or meet the same fate as all people, then the Lord has not sent me.

But if the Lord shows a new wonder, and the earth opens its mouth and swallows them, their households, and everything belonging to them, and they go down alive into the realm of the dead, you will know that these men have provoked the Lord to anger.”
When he finished speaking these words, the earth split apart beneath them.
The earth opened and swallowed them, their households, the people who were with Korah, and their livestock.
They and everything belonging to them went down alive into the realm of the dead. The earth covered them, and they perished from among the assembly.
All Israel who were around them fled at their cries, for they thought that the earth might swallow them too.
Fire came out from the Lord and consumed the two hundred and fifty men who were offering incense.
The Lord said to Moses
and to Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, “Take up the bronze censers from among those who have been burned, and scatter the strange fire away.

For the censers of these men who sinned against their own lives have become holy. Make them into hammered plates as a covering for the altar, for they were presented before the Lord and became holy. They shall be a sign to the Israelites.”
Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, took the bronze censers that those who had been burned had presented, and made them into plates for the altar.

As a reminder to the Israelites that no outsider who is not a descendant of Aaron should approach to offer incense before the Lord, lest he become like Korah and his rabble, as the Lord spoke through Moses.
The next day the Israelites grumbled against Moses and Aaron, saying, “You have killed the Lord’s people.”
When the people gathered against Moses and Aaron, they turned toward the tent of testimony. The cloud covered it, and the glory of the Lord appeared.
Moses and Aaron stood before the tent of testimony.
The Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying:
“Separate yourselves from among these people, and I will destroy them all at once.” They fell on their faces.

Moses said to Aaron, “Take the censer, put fire in it from the altar, add incense, and carry it quickly into the camp. Make atonement for them, for wrath has gone out from the Lord, and he has begun to destroy the people.”
Aaron took it as Moses had told him and ran among the people. The destruction had already begun among the people. He put in the incense and made atonement for the people.
He stood between the dead and the living, and the destruction stopped.
Those who died in the destruction numbered fourteen thousand seven hundred, besides those who died because of Korah.
Aaron returned to Moses at the entrance of the tent of testimony, and the destruction stopped.
And the Lord spoke to Moses and said:

“Speak to the Israelites and take staffs from them according to their ancestral households, from all their leaders according to the households of their clans: twelve staffs. Write each man’s name on his own staff.
Write Aaron’s name on his own staff. There shall be one staff for each tribe of Israel, which they shall give from their ancestral households.
Place them in the tent of testimony, where I will appear to you.
And the staff of the man whom I choose shall blossom, and I will remove from myself the complaints of the Israelites which they make against you.
Moses spoke to the Israelites, and all their leaders gave him their staffs, one staff for each leader according to their ancestral households: twelve staffs. Aaron’s staff was among their staffs.
Moses placed the staffs before the Lord in the tent of testimony.
The next day Moses and Aaron entered the tent of testimony, and Aaron’s staff, belonging to the house of Levi, had sprouted. It had put out a shoot, blossomed, and produced nuts.
Moses brought the staffs out from before the Lord to all the Israelites. They saw them, and each man took his own staff.
The Lord said to Moses, “Put Aaron’s staff before the testimony, to be kept as a sign for the disobedient, so that their grumbling against me may stop and they may not die.”
Moses and Aaron did just as the Lord had commanded Moses.
The Israelites spoke to Moses, saying, “Look, we are dying! We are perishing! We are being wiped out!
Everyone who approaches the Lord’s tent of testimony dies. Are we to die out completely?”

The Lord spoke to Aaron, saying, “You and your sons and your ancestral household with you shall bear the guilt associated with the sanctuary, and you and your sons shall bear the guilt associated with your priesthood.
Bring your brothers, the tribe of Levi, your father’s clan, near to you. They shall join you and serve you, while you and your sons with you shall be before the tent of testimony.
They shall attend to your duties and the duties of the tent of testimony, but they must not approach my utensils in the sanctuary or the altar, lest both they and you die.
They shall join you and keep watch over the tent of testimony, attending to all the service of the tent, and no outsider shall approach you.
You shall keep watch over the holy things and over the altar, so that wrath may no longer fall upon the Israelites.
I have taken your brothers, the Levites, from among the Israelites as substitutes given to the Lord to perform the service of the tent of testimony.

You and your sons with you shall guard your priesthood in everything concerning the altar and the area inside the curtain, and you shall perform the service of your priesthood. Any outsider who approaches shall die.

The Lord spoke to Aaron and said, “Look, I have given you charge of my firstfruits, from everything the Israelites dedicate to me. I have given them to you as an honor, and to your sons after you, as an everlasting statute.”

This shall belong to you from the consecrated holy offerings: from all their offerings, all their sacrifices, all their guilt offerings, and all their sin offerings that they give me. All these most holy things shall belong to you and your sons.
You shall eat it in the most holy place. Every male may eat it—you and your sons—for these things shall be holy to you.

This also shall belong to you from the firstfruits of their gifts, from all the offerings of the Israelites. I have given it to you and to your sons and daughters with you as a perpetual statute. Everyone who is clean in your household may eat it.
All the firstfruits of oil and all the firstfruits of wine and grain that they give to the Lord as their firstfruits, I have given to you.
All the first produce of their land that they bring to the Lord shall belong to you, and everyone who is clean in your household may eat it.
Everything dedicated by the Israelites shall belong to you.

“Everything that opens the womb among all flesh, which they offer to the Lord, whether human or animal, shall be yours. But you must redeem the firstborn of humans, and you must redeem the firstborn of unclean animals.”
