Its redemption shall take place from one month old onward, and its price shall be five shekels according to the sanctuary shekel, which is twenty obols.

But you shall not redeem the firstborn of cattle, sheep, or goats, because they are holy. You shall pour their blood against the altar and offer up their fat as an offering, a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
Their meat shall be yours; like the breast of the offering and the right thigh, it shall belong to you.

Every contribution from the holy things that the Israelites offer up to the Lord I have given to you and your children, and to your sons and daughters with you, as a perpetual statute. For it is a covenant of salt before the Lord for you and your descendants after you.
The Lord spoke to Aaron and said, “You shall receive no inheritance in their land, nor shall you have a share among them, for I am your share and your inheritance among the Israelites.”
To the sons of Levi, behold, I have given all the tithes of Israel as an inheritance in return for the service they perform in the tent of testimony.
The Israelites shall no longer approach the tent of testimony and incur sins that bring death.

“The Levites themselves shall perform the service of the tent of testimony, and they shall bear their sins. This is an everlasting statute throughout their generations, and they shall inherit no inheritance among the Israelites.”

For I have given the Levites as an inheritance the tithes of the Israelites, which they set apart as a contribution to the Lord. For this reason I said to them, “They shall inherit no allotted portion among the Israelites.”
The Lord spoke to Moses and said:

You shall speak to the Levites and say to them, “When you receive from the Israelites the tithes that I have given you, you too shall offer up from them a contribution to the Lord, a tenth of the tithe.”
Your contribution shall be reckoned to you as grain from the threshing floor and as produce from the winepress.
In this way you too shall offer up a contribution to the Lord from all your tithes that you receive from the Israelites, and from them you shall give the Lord’s contribution to Aaron the priest.
From all your gifts you shall offer up a contribution, and from all the firstfruits, the consecrated portion of them.
You shall say to them, “When you offer up the firstfruits from it, it shall be reckoned to the Levites as produce from the threshing floor and as produce from the winepress.”
You and your households may eat it anywhere, for it is your wages in return for your service in the tent of testimony.
And you will incur no sin on account of it when you take the produce from it. You must not profane the holy things of the Israelites, lest you die.
And the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying:

This is the ordinance of the law that the Lord commanded Moses, saying: Speak to the Israelites, and let them bring you a red heifer without defect, with no blemish, which has never been under a yoke.
And you shall give it to Eleazar the priest, and they shall take it outside the camp to a clean place and slaughter it before him.
And Eleazar shall take some of its blood and sprinkle its blood toward the tent of testimony seven times.
And they shall burn it before him. Its skin, its flesh, and its blood shall be burned together with its dung.
And the priest shall take fir wood, hyssop, and scarlet, and they shall throw them into the burning heifer.
And the priest shall wash his clothes and bathe his body in water, and afterward he shall enter the camp. The priest shall be unclean until evening.
And the one who burns it shall wash his clothes and bathe his body in water, and he shall be unclean until evening.

And a clean man shall gather the heifer’s ashes and heap them up outside the camp in a clean place. They shall be kept for the congregation of the Israelites for water of sprinkling, for it is for purification.

And the one who gathers the heifer’s ashes shall bathe his body and wash his clothes, and he shall be unclean until evening. This shall be a perpetual ordinance for the congregation of the Israelites and for the foreigners living among them.
Whoever comes near the corpse of any human being shall be unclean for seven days.
And he shall purify himself on the third day and on the seventh day, and then he shall be clean. But if he does not purify himself on the third day and on the seventh day, he shall not be clean.

Anyone who touches the dead body of a person who has died and does not purify himself has defiled the Lord’s tent. That person shall be cut off from Israel, because the water of sprinkling was not sprinkled on him. He is unclean, for his impurity remains in him.
And this shall be the law concerning a person who dies in a house: everyone who enters the house and everything that is in the house shall be unclean for seven days.
And every open vessel that is not covered or sealed shall be unclean.
And anyone who, in the open field, touches a wounded person, a dead person, a human bone, or a grave shall be unclean for seven days.
And for the unclean person they shall take some of the ashes of the burned purification offering and pour water over them in a vessel.

And a clean man shall take hyssop and dip it in the water, and sprinkle the house, the furnishings, the vessels, and the people who are there, and the one who has touched a human bone, a wounded person, a dead person, or a grave.

And the clean person shall sprinkle the unclean person on the third day and on the seventh day. He shall be purified on the seventh day, and shall wash his clothes and bathe his body in water, and shall be unclean until evening.

And if a person becomes unclean and does not purify himself, that person shall be cut off from his congregation, because he has defiled the Lord’s sanctuary, and the water of sprinkling was not sprinkled on him. He is unclean.
And this shall be a perpetual ordinance for you. The one who sprinkles the water of sprinkling shall wash his clothes, and the one who touches the water of sprinkling shall be unclean until evening.
And everything the unclean person touches shall be unclean until evening, and the person who touches him shall be unclean until evening.
And the Israelites, the whole congregation, came to the wilderness of Sinai in the first month, and the people camped at Kadesh. Miriam died there and was buried there.
And there was no drinking water there for the congregation, and they gathered against Moses and Aaron.
The people complained against Moses and said, “It would have been better if we had died when our brothers perished before the Lord.
Why do you bring the Lord’s people into this wilderness to kill us and our livestock?

And why do you bring us out of the land of the Egyptians to come to this bad place, a place where no seed is sown, where there are no melon plants, no vineyards, no pomegranate trees, and no water to drink?”
Moses and Aaron went away from the people to the entrance of the tent of testimony and fell on their faces, and the glory of the Lord appeared over them.
And the Lord spoke to Moses and said:

“Take the staff and assemble the people, you and Aaron your brother. Speak to the rock in their presence, and it will give its water. Bring water out of the rock for them, and give the people and their livestock water to drink.”
Moses took the staff from before the Lord, as the Lord had commanded him.
Moses and Aaron assembled the people before the rock, and he said to them, “Listen to me, you unbelievers! Shall we bring water out of this rock for you?”
Moses raised his hand and struck the rock twice with the staff. Much water came out, and the people and their livestock drank.
The Lord said to Moses and Aaron, “Because you did not believe in me and show me to be holy before the Israelites, you will not bring this people into the land that I have given them.”
This is the Water of Complaints, because the Israelites complained before the Lord, and he showed himself to be holy among them.
Moses sent messengers from Kadesh to the king of Edom, saying, “This is what your brother Israel says: You yourself know all the hardships that have befallen us,
and how our fathers went down to Egypt, and we lived as foreigners in Egypt for many days. The Egyptians mistreated us and our fathers.
We cried out to the Lord, and the Lord heard our voice and sent an angel who brought us out of Egypt. Now we are in Kadesh, a city at the edge of your territory.

Now let us pass through your land. We will not pass through your fields or your vineyards, and we will not drink water from your wells. We will travel along the king’s highway and will not turn to the right or the left until we have passed beyond your territory.”
Edom said to him, “You shall not pass through my land. Otherwise, I will come out against you in battle.”
The Israelites said to him, “We will pass along your mountain. If I and my flocks drink any of your water, we will pay you its price. It is no trouble; let us pass along your mountain.”
But he said, “You shall not pass through my land.” And Edom came out against them with a great multitude and a mighty force.
Edom was unwilling to let Israel pass through his territory, and Israel turned away from him.
They set out from Kadesh, and the Israelites, the whole community, came to Mount Hor.
The Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron on Mount Hor, at the border of the land of the Edomites, saying:
“Aaron shall be gathered to his people, for he shall not enter the land that I have given the Israelites, because you angered me at the Water of Complaints.
Take Aaron and his son Eleazar and bring them up Mount Hor in the sight of all the people.
Remove Aaron’s robe and put it on his son Eleazar. Aaron shall be gathered to his people and die there.”
Moses did as the Lord had commanded him and brought him up Mount Hor before all the people.
He removed Aaron’s garments and put them on his son Eleazar. Aaron died on the summit of the mountain, and Moses and Eleazar came down from the mountain.
And all the people saw that Aaron had died, and the whole house of Israel mourned Aaron for thirty days.
And the Canaanite king of Arad, who lived beside the wilderness, heard that Israel had come by the road of Atharim. He fought against Israel and took some of them captive.
And Israel made a vow to the Lord, saying, “If you deliver this nation into my hands, I will put it and its cities under the ban of destruction.”
And the Lord heard Israel’s voice and delivered the Canaanites into their hands. Israel put them and their cities under the ban of destruction, and called that place Destruction.
And they set out from Mount Hor by the road to the Red Sea and went around Edom, and the people grew weary on the journey.
And the people spoke against God and Moses, saying, “Why did you bring us out of Egypt to kill us in this wilderness? There is no bread and no water, and we are sick of this worthless bread.”
And the Lord sent deadly snakes among the people, and they bit the people, and many of the Israelites died.

And they came to Moses and said, “We have sinned, because we have spoken evil of the Lord and of you. Now pray to the Lord, and let him take these snakes away from us.” And Moses prayed to the Lord for the people.
And the Lord said to Moses, “Make yourself a snake and put it on a pole. Whenever a snake bites someone, every person bitten who looks at it will live.”
And Moses made a bronze snake and placed it on the pole. Whenever a snake bit someone, that person looked at the bronze snake and lived.
And the Israelites set out and came and camped at Oboth.
And they set out from Oboth and camped at Achel-gai, beyond the wilderness that faces Moab on the eastern side.
From there they set out and camped in the valley of Zered.
And they set out from there and camped beyond the Arnon, in the wilderness extending from the borders of the Amorites. For the Arnon is the boundary of Moab, between the Moabites and the Amorites.
For this reason it is said in the book of the War of the Lord: “He set Zoob on fire, and the valley of the Arnon,
and established the inhabited valleys at Ar, and it lies beside the borders of Moab.”
And from there, beyond it, was the Well. This is the well about which the Lord said to Moses, “Gather the people, and I will give them water to drink.”
Then Israel sang this song of praise over the well: “Sing to it,
the well that princes dug and the kings of the nations hewed out during their kingship and their rule.”
And from the well they went to Mattanah, and from Mattanah to Manael, and from Manael to Bamoth,
and from Bamoth to Anaen, which is in the plain of Moab, at the top of the hewn rock that overlooks the wilderness.
And Moses sent messengers to the king of the Amorites with words of peace, saying,

“Let us pass through your land. We will travel along the road. We will turn aside neither into fields nor into vineyards, and we will not drink water from your wells. We will follow the king’s highway until we have passed beyond your borders.”
And Sihon did not allow Israel to pass through his territory. Sihon gathered all his people and went out into the wilderness to fight against Israel. He came to Jahaz and fought against Israel.
And Israel struck him down with the sword and took possession of his land from the Arnon to the Jabbok, as far as the Ammonites, for Jazer is the boundary of the Ammonites.
And Israel took all those cities and settled in all the cities of the Amorites, in Heshbon and all its surrounding settlements.
For Heshbon was the city of Sihon, king of the Amorites. He had previously fought against the king of Moab and taken all his land from Aroer to the Arnon.
Therefore the proverb-makers say: Come to Heshbon, for the city of Sihon has been built and made ready.
For fire came out of Heshbon, and a flame from the city of Sihon. It consumed as far as Moab and devoured the pillars of the Arnon.
Woe to you, Moab! You have perished, people of Chemosh! Their sons were given over to flight, and their daughters to captivity under the king of the Amorites.
And their offspring will be destroyed from Heshbon to Dibon, and their women were set ablaze with fire in Moab.
And Israel settled in all the cities of the Amorites.
And Moses sent men to spy out Jazer. They captured it and its villages and drove out the Amorite who lived there.
And they set out again along the road to Bashan. Og, king of Bashan, came out against them with all his people to fight at Edrei.

And the Lord said to Moses: Do not be afraid of him, for I have delivered him into your hands, together with all his people and all his land. You shall do to him as you did to Sihon, king of the Amorites, who lived in Heshbon.
And he struck him, his sons, and all his people until none of them remained alive, and they took possession of their land.
And the Israelites moved on and camped in the western parts of Moab, beside the Jordan, opposite Jericho.
And Balak, son of Zippor, saw everything that Israel had done to the Amorite.
Moab was very afraid of the people because they were numerous, and Moab dreaded the Israelites.
And Moab said to the elders of Midian: Now this people will lick up everything around us, as an ox licks up the green plants in the field. And Balak, son of Zippor, was king of Moab at that time.

And he sent messengers to Balaam, son of Beor, at Pethor, which was beside the river in the land of his own people, to summon him and say: Look, a nation has come out of Egypt and covered the face of the land, and it is settled near me.

Now come and curse this people for me, for they are stronger than I am. Perhaps we will be able to strike some of them down, and I will drive them out of my land. For I know that whoever you bless is blessed, and whoever you curse is cursed.
The elders of Moab and the elders of Midian went with [?] in their hands. They came to Balaam and told him Balak’s message.
And he said to them: Stay here tonight, and I will give you an answer according to whatever the Lord tells me. And the princes of Moab stayed with Balaam.
And God came to Balaam and said to him: Who are these men with you?
And Balaam said to God: Balak, son of Zippor, king of Moab, sent them to me and said:

Look, a nation has come out of Egypt and covered the face of the land, and it is settled near me. Now come and curse them for me. Perhaps I will be able to strike them down and drive them out of my land.
God said to Balaam, “Do not go with them, and do not curse the people, because they are blessed.”
And Balaam rose in the morning and said to Balak’s princes: Go back to your lord, for God will not allow me to go with you.
And the princes of Moab rose and came to Balak and said: Balaam would not come with us.
And Balak again sent princes, more numerous and more distinguished than the others.
They came to Balaam and said to him: Thus says Balak, son of Zippor: I beg you, do not delay in coming to me.
For I will honor you greatly and do whatever you tell me. Now come and curse this people for me.
Balaam answered and said to Balak’s officials, “Even if Balak gives me his house full of silver and gold, I cannot go beyond the word of the Lord God to do anything small or great of my own accord.”
“Now stay here tonight, and I will find out what more the Lord will say to me.”
God came to Balaam during the night and said to him, “If these men have come to summon you, get up and go with them. But do only what I tell you.”
Balaam rose in the morning, saddled his donkey, and went with the officials of Moab.
God became furious because he was going, and the angel of God stood in his way to oppose him. He was riding his donkey, and his two young servants were with him.

When the donkey saw the angel of God standing against him in the road with a drawn sword in his hand, the donkey turned off the road and went into the field. He struck the donkey with a staff to turn it back onto the road.
The angel of God stood in a passage between the vineyards, with a fence on this side and a fence on that side.
When the donkey saw the angel of God, it pressed itself against the wall and crushed Balaam’s foot, and he beat it again.
The angel of God went farther and stood in a narrow place where there was no room to turn aside to the right or the left.
When the donkey saw the angel of God, it lay down under Balaam. Balaam became angry and struck the donkey with his staff.
God opened the donkey’s mouth, and it said to Balaam, “What have I done to you that you have struck me these three times?”
Balaam said to the donkey, “Because you have made a fool of me! If I had a sword in my hand, I would have struck you by now.”
The donkey said to Balaam, “Am I not your donkey, which you have ridden from your youth until this very day? Have I ever neglected you by acting this way toward you?” He said, “No.”
God opened Balaam’s eyes, and he saw the angel of the Lord blocking his way on the road, with a drawn sword in his hand. He fell on his face and bowed down to him.
The angel of God said to him, “Why have you struck your donkey these three times? Look, I have come out to oppose you, because your way is not right before me.”
“Your donkey saw me and turned away from me these three times. If it had not turned away from me, I would by now have killed you and spared it.”
Balaam said to the angel of the Lord, “I have sinned, for I did not know that you were standing against me in the road. Now, if this displeases you, I will turn back.”
The angel of God said to Balaam, “Go with these men, but take care to speak only the word that I tell you.” So Balaam went with Balak’s officials.
When Balak heard that Balaam was coming, he went out to meet him at the city of Moab, which is on the border of the Arnon, at the edge of the territory.
Balak said to Balaam, “Did I not send to summon you? Why did you not come to me? Was I perhaps unable to honor you?”
Balaam said to Balak, “Here I am; I have come to you. But can I now say anything? I will speak only what God puts in my mouth.”
Balaam went with Balak and came to the towns of the encampments.
Balak slaughtered cattle and sheep and sent some to Balaam and the officials who were with him.
When morning came, Balak took Balaam with him and brought him up to the pillar of Baal. From there he showed him a portion of the people.
Balaam said to Balak, “Build me seven altars here, and prepare seven bulls and seven rams for me here.”
Balak did as Balaam told him, and offered a bull and a ram on the altar.

Balaam said to Balak, “Stand beside your sacrifice, and I will go. Perhaps God will come to meet me and appear to me. Whatever he reveals to me, I will tell you.” Balak stood beside his sacrifice, and Balaam went to inquire of God, going straight ahead.
God appeared to Balaam, and Balaam said to him, “I have prepared seven altars and offered a bull and a ram on each altar.”
God put a word in Balaam’s mouth and said, “Return to Balak and speak in this way.”
And he returned to him, and he was standing beside his burnt offerings, with all the princes of Moab.

And the Spirit of God came upon him, and he took up his oracle and said: “Balak, king of Moab, summoned me from Mesopotamia, from the mountains of the east, and said: ‘Come, curse Jacob for me; come, call down a curse on Israel for me.’”
“How can I curse someone whom God does not curse? Or how can I call down a curse on someone whom the Lord does not curse?
For I saw him from the mountains, and from the hills I looked at him beforehand. Look, a people will dwell alone and will not be counted among the nations.
Who has precisely counted Jacob’s descendants, and who will count Israel’s companies? May my soul die among the souls of the righteous, and may my descendants be like their descendants.”
And Balak said to Balaam: “What have you done to me? I summoned you to curse my enemies, but you have blessed them with a blessing!”
And Balaam said to Balak: “Must I not take care to speak whatever God puts into my mouth?”

And Balak said to him: “Come with me again to another place, from which you will not see them all. You will see only a portion of them, and you will not see all of them. Curse them for me from there.”
And he took him to the fields of the lookout, to the summit of the hewn rock. He built seven altars there and offered a bull and a ram on an altar.
And Balaam said to Balak: “Stand beside your sacrifice, and I will go to consult God.”
And God met Balaam and put a word into his mouth, and said: “Return to Balak and speak in this way.”
He returned to him, and he was standing beside his burnt offering, with all the rulers of Moab beside him. Balak said to him, “What did the Lord say?”
And he took up his oracle and said: “Rise, Balak, and listen; give ear, you witness, son of Zippor.
God is not like a man, to [?], nor like a son of man, to be threatened. You said: ‘Will he not do it? Will he speak and not carry it out?’
Look, I have received the command to bless. I will bless and will not reverse it.
There will be no hardship in Jacob, and no toil will appear among Israel. The Lord their God is with them; the glories of rulers are among them.
And God, who brought them out of Egypt, is over them like the glory of a unicorn.
For there is no enchantment in Jacob and no divination among Israel. In due time Jacob and Israel will be told what God is going to accomplish.
Look, the people will rise like a lion’s cub and stride proudly like a lion. They will not sleep until they have eaten prey and drunk the blood of the wounded.”
And Balak said to Balaam: “Do not curse them for me at all, and do not bless them at all.”
Balaam answered and said to Balak: “Did I not speak to you and say, ‘Whatever God tells me, that I will do’?”
And Balak said to Balaam: “Come, I will take you to another place. Perhaps it will please God, and you will curse them for me from there.”
And Balak took Balaam to the summit of Peor, which overlooks the wilderness.
And Balaam said to Balak: “Build me seven altars here, and prepare seven bulls and seven rams for me here.”
And Balak did as Balaam had told him, and offered a bull and a ram on an altar.
When Balaam saw that it pleased the Lord to bless Israel, he did not go to seek omens as he usually did, but turned his face toward the wilderness.
And Balaam raised his eyes and saw Israel camped tribe by tribe, and the Spirit of God came upon him.
And he took up his oracle and said: “Balaam son of Beor speaks; the man who sees truly speaks,
who saw the vision of God in sleep, with his eyes open:
How beautiful are your houses, Jacob, and your tents, Israel!
Like shady forests, like gardens beside rivers, like tents that the Lord set up, and like cedars beside flowing waters.
A man will come forth from his offspring and rule over many nations. His kingdom will be exalted above Gog, and his kingdom will grow.
God led him out of Egypt; the majesty of a unicorn rests upon him. He will devour the nations that are his enemies, suck the marrow from their fat, and shoot his arrows at his enemies.
He crouched and rested like a lion and like a lion’s cub. Who will rouse him? Those who bless you will be blessed, and those who curse you will be cursed.”
Balak became angry with Balaam and struck his hands together. Balak said to Balaam, “I called you to curse my enemies, but look, you have blessed him these three times!
Now flee to your own place! I said I would honor you, but the Lord has deprived you of honor.”
Balaam said to Balak, “Did I not also speak to your messengers whom you sent to me and say,
‘Even if Balak gives me his house full of silver and gold, I cannot go beyond the word of the Lord to do anything evil or good on my own. Whatever God says, that I will speak’?
Now, look, I am going to my own place. Come, I will advise you about what this people will do to your people in the last days.”
And he took up his oracle and said: “Balaam son of Beor speaks; the man who sees truly speaks,
who heard the words of God, knows the knowledge of the Most High, and saw the vision of God in sleep, with his eyes open:

I will show him, but not now; I will call him blessed, but not soon. A star will rise from Jacob, and a man will arise from Israel. He will strike the rulers of Moab and take all the sons of Seth as plunder.
Edom, belonging to Esau his enemy, shall become his inheritance, and Israel acted mightily.
A man will arise from Jacob and destroy the survivors from the city.”
When he saw Amalek, he took up his oracle and said: “Amalek is the foremost of the nations, but their offspring will perish.”
When he saw the Kenite, he took up his oracle and said: “Your dwelling is strong, even if you set your nest in caves.
Even if the nest of your deceit is in Beor, the Assyrians will take you captive.”
And he took up his oracle and said: “Who will live when God brings this about?
He will come forth from the hands of the Kittim, and they will afflict Asshur and afflict the Hebrews, and they themselves will perish together.”
Balaam rose, turned back, and went to his own place, and Balak went his own way.
Israel camped at Shittim, and the people defiled themselves by committing sexual immorality with the daughters of Moab.
They invited them to the sacrifices of their idols, and the people ate from their sacrifices and bowed down to their idols.
Israel devoted itself to Baal-peor, and the Lord’s anger blazed against Israel.
And the Lord said to Moses, “Take all the leaders of this people and hang them before the Lord in the sunlight, so that the Lord’s fierce anger may turn away from Israel.”
And Moses said to the tribes of Israel, “Each of you must kill his own kinsmen who have devoted themselves to Baal of Peor.”

And behold, an Israelite man came, bringing his brother to a Midianite woman in the sight of Moses and in the sight of the whole congregation of the Israelites. They were weeping at the entrance to the tent of testimony.
When Phinehas, son of Eleazar, son of Aaron the priest, saw this, he rose from among the congregation and took a spear in his hand.
He went into the furnace after the Israelite man and pierced both of them, the Israelite man and the woman, through her womb. And the plague among the Israelites stopped.
Those who died from the plague numbered twenty-four thousand.
And the Lord spoke to Moses and said:
“Phinehas, son of Eleazar, son of Aaron the priest, turned my anger away from the Israelites by arousing my zeal among them, and I did not destroy the Israelites in my zeal.
Therefore say this: ‘Behold, I give him a covenant of peace.
It shall be for him and his descendants after him a covenant of everlasting priesthood, because he was zealous for his God and made atonement for the Israelites.’”
The name of the Israelite man who was struck down with the Midianite woman was Zimri son of Salu, a leader of an ancestral house of the descendants of Simeon.
The name of the Midianite woman who was struck down was Cozbi, daughter of Zur, chief of the nation of Ommoth, of an ancestral house in Midian.
And the Lord spoke to Moses and said:
“Speak to the Israelites and say, ‘Be hostile to the Midianites and strike them down,

for they are hostile to you through the deceit with which they deceived you concerning Peor and Cozbi, the daughter of the leader of Midian, their sister, who was struck down on the day of the plague because of Peor.’”
After the plague, the Lord spoke to Moses and to Eleazar the priest, saying:
“Take a census of the whole congregation of the Israelites, from twenty years old and upward, by their ancestral houses—everyone in Israel who can go out to war.”
Moses and Eleazar the priest spoke in Araboth of Moab, beside the Jordan opposite Jericho, saying:
“From twenty years old and upward, as the Lord commanded Moses—you and the Israelites who came out of Egypt, prepare yourselves.”
Reuben was Israel’s firstborn. The sons of Reuben were Hanoch and the clan of Hanoch, and Pallu and the clan of Pallu.
Hezron and the clan of Hezron; Carmi and the clan of Carmi.
These are the clans of Reuben, and their census numbered forty-three thousand seven hundred and thirty.
The son of Pallu was Eliab.

The sons of Eliab were Nemuel, Dathan, and Abiram. These were prominent men of the congregation, and these were the ones who rose against Moses and Aaron in the congregation of Korah, which rose in opposition to the Lord.
The earth opened its mouth and swallowed them and Korah as his congregation perished, when fire consumed the two hundred and fifty, and they became a warning.
But the sons of Korah did not die.
The sons of Simeon and the clans of the sons of Simeon were Nemuel and the clan of Nemuel, Jamin and the clan of Jamin, and Jachin and the clan of Jachin;
Zerah and the clan of Zerah, and Shaul and the clan of Shaul.
These are the clans of Simeon, numbering twenty-two thousand two hundred in their census.
The sons of Gad according to their clans were Zephon and the clan of Zephon, Haggi and the clan of Haggi, and Shuni and the clan of Shuni.
Ozni and the clan of Ozni; Addi and the clan of Addi; Arod and the clan of Arod.
Ariel and the clan of Ariel.
These are the clans of the sons of Gad, numbering forty-four thousand five hundred at their muster.
The sons of Judah were Er, Onan, Shelah, Perez, and Zerah. Er and Onan died in the land of the Canaanites.
The sons of Judah, according to their clans, were Shelah and the clan of Shelah; Perez and the clan of Perez; Zerah and the clan of Zerah.
The sons of Perez were Hezron and the clan of Hezron; Hamul and the clan of Hamul.
These are the clans of Judah, numbering seventy-six thousand five hundred at their muster.
The sons of Issachar according to their clans: Tola and the clan of Tola; Puah and the clan of Puah; Jashub and the clan of Jashub.
Shimron and the clan of Shimron.
These are the clans of Issachar, numbering sixty-four thousand three hundred in their census.
The sons of Zebulun, according to their clans, were Sered and the clan of Sered; Elon and the clan of Elon; Jahleel and the clan of Jahleel.
These are the clans of Zebulun, numbering sixty thousand five hundred at their muster.
The sons of Joseph, according to their clans, were Manasseh and Ephraim.
The sons of Manasseh were Machir and the clan of Machir. Machir fathered Gilead: Gilead and the clan of Gilead.
The sons of Gilead were Achiezer and the clan of Achiezer; Helek and the clan of Helek.
Asriel and the clan of Asriel; Shechem and the clan of Shechem.
Shemida and the clan of Shemida; Hepher and the clan of Hepher.
Zelophehad son of Hepher had no sons, but daughters. The names of Zelophehad’s daughters were Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.
These are the clans of Manasseh, numbering fifty-two thousand seven hundred at their muster.
These are the sons of Ephraim: Shuthelah and the clan of Shuthelah; Tahan and the clan of Tahan.
These are the sons of Shuthelah: Eden and the clan of Eden.
These are the clans of Ephraim, numbering thirty-two thousand five hundred at their muster. These are the clans of Joseph, according to their clans.
The sons of Benjamin, according to their clans, were Bela and the clan of Bela; Ashbel and the clan of Ashbel; Ahiram and the clan of Ahiram.
Shupham and the clan of Shupham.
The sons of Bela were Ard and Naaman, and the clan of Naaman.
These are the sons of Benjamin, according to their clans, numbering thirty-five thousand five hundred at their muster.
The sons of Dan, according to their clans, were Shuham and the clan of Shuham. These are the clans of Dan, according to their clans.
All the clans of Shuham, according to their census, numbered sixty-four thousand six hundred.
The sons of Asher, according to their clans, were Jimnah and the clan of Jimnah, Ishui and the clan of Ishui, Beriah and the clan of Beriah;
Heber and the clan of Heber, Malchiel and the clan of Malchiel.
The name of Asher’s daughter was Serah.
These are the clans of Asher; according to their census, they numbered forty-three thousand six hundred.
The sons of Naphtali according to their clans: Jahzeel and the clan of Jahzeel; Guni and the clan of Guni.
Jezer and the clan of Jezer, Shillem and the clan of Shillem.
These are the clans of Naphtali; according to their census, they numbered forty thousand three hundred.
This is the census of the Israelites: six hundred and one thousand seven hundred thirty.
And the Lord spoke to Moses and said:
To these the land shall be divided as an inheritance according to the number of names.

For the larger group you shall increase the inheritance, and for the smaller group you shall reduce their inheritance. Each shall receive their inheritance according to the number counted in the census.
The land shall be inherited by lot. They shall inherit according to the names of the tribes of their forefathers.
By lot they shall divide their inheritance between the larger and smaller groups.
The sons of Levi, according to their clans, were Gershon and the clan of Gershon, Kohath and the clan of Kohath, Merari and the clan of Merari.
These also are the clans of the sons of Levi: the clan of Libni, the clan of Hebron, the clan of Korah, and the clan of Mushi. Kohath fathered Amram.
The name of his wife was Jochebed, daughter of Levi, who bore these to Levi in Egypt. She bore Aaron and Moses and their sister Miriam to Amram.
To Aaron were born Nadab and Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar.
Nadab and Abihu died when they offered unauthorized fire before the Lord in the wilderness of Sinai.

Those counted in their census numbered twenty-three thousand, every male one month old and above. They were not counted in the census among the Israelites, because no allotment had been given to them among the Israelites.
This is the census taken by Moses and Eleazar the priest, who counted the Israelites in Araboth of Moab, by the Jordan opposite Jericho.
Among them there was not one man who had been counted by Moses and Aaron when they took the census of the Israelites in the wilderness of Sinai.
For the Lord had said of them, “They shall surely die in the wilderness.” Not one of them remained except Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun.

The daughters of Zelophehad son of Hepher, son of Gilead, son of Machir, from the clan of Manasseh among the sons of Joseph, came forward. These are their names: Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.
They stood before Moses, before Eleazar the priest, before the leaders, and before all the people at the entrance of the tent of testimony, and said:
“Our father died there in the wilderness. He was not among the people who gathered before the Lord in Korah’s company, but died because of his own sins, and he had no sons.
Now let our father’s name not be erased from among his tribe because he had no son. Give us an inheritance among our father’s brothers.”
Moses brought their case before the Lord.
And the Lord spoke to Moses and said:
“The daughters of Zelophehad have spoken rightly. You must give them property as an inheritance among their father’s brothers, and transfer their father’s allotted share to them.”
And you shall speak to the Israelites and say: If a man dies and has no son, let him give his inheritance to his daughter.
And if he has no daughter, you shall give his inheritance to his brother.
And if he has no brothers, you shall give his inheritance to his paternal uncle.

And if his father has no brothers, you shall give the inheritance to his nearest relative within his tribe, and he shall inherit his property. This shall be a legal ordinance for the Israelites, as the Lord commanded Moses.
And the Lord said to Moses: Go up to the mountain on the other side, to Mount Nebo, and see the land of the Canaanites, which I will give to the Israelites as a possession.
You shall see it, and you too shall be gathered to your people, as Aaron your brother was gathered on Mount Hor.

For you disobeyed my word in the wilderness of Zin when the people disputed: you were to show me to be holy, but you did not show me to be holy at the waters before them. These are the Waters of Dispute in the wilderness of Zin.
And Moses said to the Lord:
“May the Lord, the God of the spirits of all flesh, appoint a man over this congregation.”
Who will go out before them and who will lead them out and bring them in, so that the Lord’s people may not be like sheep without a shepherd.
And the Lord spoke to Moses and said: Take Joshua son of Nun, a man in whom is the Spirit, and lay your hands on him.
And you shall set him before Eleazar the priest and instruct him before all the people, and you shall give commands concerning him before them.
And you shall place some of your glory upon him, so that the Israelites will listen to him.

And he shall stand before Eleazar the priest, and they shall ask him for the judgments of revelation before the Lord. At his word they shall go out, and at his word they shall come in: he and the Israelites together, and all the people.
And Moses did as the Lord commanded him. He took Joshua and set him before Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, and before all the people.
And he laid his hands on him and commissioned him, as the Lord commanded Moses.
And the Lord spoke to Moses and said:
Command the Israelites and say to them: You shall take care to present my sacrifices, my food, and my gifts as a pleasing aroma at my appointed festivals.
“You shall say to them: These are the offerings that you shall present to the Lord: two lambs without blemish every day, as a continual burnt offering.”
You shall offer one lamb in the morning, and you shall offer the second lamb in the evening.
And you shall offer one tenth of an ephah of fine flour mixed with one quarter of a hin of pressed oil.
It is a continual burnt offering, as it was on Mount Sinai, as a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
And its drink offering shall be one quarter of a hin for each lamb. In the holy place you shall pour out the drink offering to the Lord.
And you shall offer the second lamb in the evening. You shall offer it with its grain offering and its drink offering as a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
And on the Sabbath day you shall present two unblemished one-year-old lambs and two tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil as a grain offering.
And the drink offering of the Sabbath burnt offering, Sabbath by Sabbath, shall be in addition to the daily burnt offering and its drink offering.
And at the beginning of each month you shall present burnt offerings to the Lord: two young bulls from the herd, one ram, and seven unblemished one-year-old lambs.
And three tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil for each bull, and two tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil for each ram.
And a tenth of fine flour mixed with oil for each lamb, as an offering to the Lord with a pleasing aroma.

Their drink offering shall be half a hin of wine for each bull, a third of a hin for each ram, and a quarter of a hin for each lamb. These shall be the burnt offerings month by month throughout the months of the year.
And one male goat shall be offered to the Lord for their sins, in addition to the regular burnt offering and its drink offering.
In the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month, is the Lord’s Passover.
On the fifteenth day of that same month is a feast. You shall eat unleavened bread for seven days.
On the first day you shall have a holy assembly. You shall do no ordinary work.
You shall present burnt offerings and offerings to the Lord: two bulls from the herd, one ram, and seven year-old lambs without blemish.
Their grain offering shall be fine flour mixed with oil: three tenths for each bull and two tenths for each ram.
You shall provide one tenth for each lamb, for all seven lambs.
And one male goat as a sin offering, to make atonement for them.
These are in addition to the regular morning burnt offering, which is the continual burnt offering.

You shall do this in the same manner each day for seven days: an offering, a burnt offering with a pleasing aroma to the Lord. You shall offer its drink offering in addition to the regular burnt offering.
On the seventh day you shall have a holy assembly. You shall do no ordinary work on it.
On the day of the firstfruits, when you present a grain offering to the Lord at the Feast of Weeks, you shall have a holy assembly. You shall do no ordinary work.
You shall present burnt offerings with a pleasing aroma to the Lord: two bulls from the herd, one ram, and seven year-old lambs without blemish.
Their grain offering shall be fine flour mixed with oil: three tenths for each bull and two tenths for each ram.
And a tenth for each lamb of the seven lambs.
And one male goat as a sin offering, to make atonement for you.
You shall offer these in addition to the regular burnt offering and their grain offerings and drink offerings. They shall be without blemish for you.
In the seventh month, on the first day of the month, you shall have a holy assembly. You shall do no ordinary work. It shall be a day of sounding the signal for you.
You shall offer burnt offerings with a pleasing aroma to the Lord: one bull from the herd, one ram, and seven year-old lambs without blemish.
Their grain offering shall be fine flour mixed with oil: three tenths for each bull and two tenths for each ram.
And a tenth for each lamb of the seven lambs.
And one male goat as a sin offering, to make atonement for you.
These are in addition to the burnt offering for the new moon and their grain offerings and drink offerings, according to their prescribed requirements, with a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
On the tenth day of that same month you shall have a holy assembly. You shall humble yourselves and do no ordinary work.
You shall present burnt offerings with a pleasing aroma, offerings to the Lord: one bull from the herd, one ram, and seven year-old lambs without blemish.
And their grain offering: fine flour mixed with oil, three tenths for each bull and two tenths for each ram.
And a tenth for each lamb of the seven lambs.

And one male goat as a sin offering to make atonement for you, besides the offering for sin and atonement, the regular burnt offerings, their grain offering, and their drink offering according to its prescribed rule, as a fragrant offering to the Lord.
On the fifteenth day of that same seventh month, you shall have a holy assembly. You shall do no ordinary work, and you shall celebrate it as a festival to the Lord for seven days.
On the first day, you shall offer burnt offerings, gifts of a pleasing aroma to the Lord: thirteen young bulls from the herd, two rams, and fourteen year-old lambs. They shall be without blemish.
And their grain offerings: fine flour mixed with oil, three tenths for each of the thirteen bulls and two tenths for each of the two rams.
And one tenth for each of the fourteen lambs.
And one male goat as a sin offering, besides the regular burnt offerings and their sacrifices and drink offerings.
On the second day: twelve bulls, two rams, and fourteen unblemished year-old lambs.
And their grain offerings and drink offerings for the bulls, the rams, and the lambs, according to their number and their prescribed rules.
And one male goat as a sin offering, besides the regular burnt offering, their grain offerings, and their drink offerings.
On the third day: eleven bulls, two rams, and fourteen unblemished year-old lambs.
And their grain offering and drink offering for the bulls, the rams, and the lambs, according to their number.
And one male goat as a sin offering, besides their regular burnt offerings and their drink offerings.
On the fourth day: ten bulls, two rams, and fourteen unblemished year-old lambs.
And their grain offerings and drink offerings for the bulls, the rams, and the lambs, according to their number and their prescribed rules.
And one male goat as a sin offering, besides the regular burnt offerings, their grain offerings, and their drink offerings.
On the fifth day: nine bulls, two rams, and fourteen unblemished year-old sheep.
And their grain offerings and drink offerings for the bulls, the rams, and the lambs, according to their number and their prescribed rules.
And one male goat as a sin offering, besides the regular burnt offerings, their grain offerings, and their drink offerings.
On the sixth day: eight bulls, two rams, and fourteen unblemished year-old lambs.
And their grain offerings and drink offerings for the bulls, the rams, and the lambs, according to their number and their prescribed rules.
And one male goat as a sin offering, besides the regular burnt offerings, their grain offerings, and their drink offerings.
On the seventh day: seven bulls, two rams, and fourteen unblemished year-old lambs.
And their grain offerings and drink offerings for the bulls, the rams, and the lambs, according to their number and their prescribed rules.
And one male goat as a sin offering, besides the regular burnt offerings, their grain offerings, and their drink offerings.
On the eighth day you shall have a closing observance. You shall do no ordinary work on it.
And you shall present burnt offerings as fragrant offerings to the Lord: one bull, one ram, and seven unblemished year-old lambs.
And their grain offerings and drink offerings for the bull, the ram, and the lambs, according to their number and their prescribed rules.
And one male goat as a sin offering, besides the regular burnt offerings, their grain offerings, and their drink offerings.
You shall offer these to the Lord at your festivals, besides your vows, your burnt offerings, your freewill offerings, your grain offerings, your drink offerings, and your peace offerings.
And Moses spoke to the Israelites as the Lord had commanded Moses.
And Moses spoke to the leaders of the Israelites and said, “This is what the Lord has commanded:
If a man makes a vow to the Lord, or swears an oath with a binding pledge, or places an obligation on himself, he shall not break his word, but shall do everything that comes from his mouth.
And if a woman makes a vow to the Lord or places some obligation on herself while she is young and in her father’s house,

and her father hears her vows and the obligations she has placed on herself, and her father says nothing to her, all her vows shall stand, and all the obligations she has placed on herself shall remain binding on her.

But if her father does not consent on the day he hears of it, none of her vows or the obligations she has imposed on herself shall stand. The Lord shall release her from guilt, because her father did not consent.
But if she marries while her vows are still binding on her, according to the vow spoken by her lips by which she placed an obligation on herself,
and her husband hears and says nothing to her on the day he hears, then all her vows shall stand, and the obligations she has placed on herself shall remain binding.

But if her husband does not consent on the day he hears, none of her vows or the obligations she has placed on herself shall remain binding, because her husband did not consent, and the Lord shall absolve her.
And the vows of a widow or a divorced woman, by which she binds herself, shall remain binding on her.
But if her vows are made in her husband’s house, or she places an obligation on herself by an oath,
and her husband hears and says nothing to her and consents, all her vows shall stand, and all the obligations she has placed on herself shall remain binding on her.

But if her husband annuls them on the day he hears of them, nothing that has come from her lips concerning her vows or the obligations she has imposed on herself shall be binding on her, because her husband has canceled them. The Lord shall release her from guilt.
Her husband may confirm or annul any vow and any binding oath by which she undertakes to afflict herself.
And if he continues to say nothing to her from day to day, he confirms all her vows and makes her obligations binding on her, because he said nothing to her on the day he heard.
And if her husband annuls them after the day he heard, he shall bear his guilt.
These are the statutes that the Lord commanded Moses concerning a husband and his wife, and a father and his daughter while she is young and in her father’s house.”
And the Lord spoke to Moses and said:
“Take vengeance on the Midianites for the Israelites, and afterward you shall be gathered to your people.”
And Moses spoke to the people and said, “Arm men from among you to fight before the Lord against Midian, to carry out the Lord’s vengeance on Midian.
Send a thousand men from each of the tribes of Israel to wage war.”
And from the thousands of Israel, a thousand men from each tribe were counted out: twelve thousand armed for war.

And Moses sent them out, a thousand men from each tribe with their military force, together with Phinehas son of Eleazar, son of Aaron the priest, with the sacred vessels and the trumpets for sounding the alarm in their hands.
And they fought against the Midianites as the Lord had commanded Moses, and killed every male.

And they killed the kings of the Midianites along with their wounded: Evi, Zur, Rekem, Hur, and Reba, the five kings of Midian. They also killed Balaam son of Beor with the sword, along with their wounded.
And they took the women of Midian, their households, their livestock, all their possessions, and their wealth as plunder.
And they burned all their cities with their houses, and all their villages.
And they took all their spoils and all their plunder, from people to livestock.
And they brought the captives, the plunder, and the spoils to Moses, Eleazar the priest, and all the Israelites, to the camp at Araboth of Moab, opposite Jericho, beside the Jordan.
And Moses, Eleazar the priest, and all the leaders of the people went out to meet them outside the camp.
And Moses was angry with the officers of the army, the commanders of thousands and the commanders of hundreds who had returned from battle.
Moses said to them, “Why have you kept all the females alive?”
For they were the ones who, following Balaam’s words, caused the Israelites to go astray and despise the word of the Lord concerning Peor, and a plague came upon the Lord’s people.
Now kill every male among all the children, and kill every woman who has known sexual relations with a man.
But keep alive all the female children who have not known sexual relations with a man.
And you shall stay outside the camp for seven days. Everyone who has killed someone or touched a slain person shall purify himself on the third day and on the seventh day, both you and your captives.
And you shall purify every garment, every leather article, everything made of hair, and every wooden article.
And Eleazar the priest said to the men of the army who had returned from battle, “These are the requirements of the law that the Lord commanded Moses:
Except for gold, silver, bronze, iron, lead, and tin,
everything that passes through fire shall be purified, but it shall also be purified with the water of sprinkling. And everything that does not pass through fire shall be washed with water.
You shall wash your garments on the seventh day and be clean, and afterward you shall enter the camp.”
And the Lord spoke to Moses and said:
“Count the captured spoils, from people to livestock—you, Eleazar the priest, and the leaders of the ancestral houses of the people.
And divide the spoils between the fighting men who went out to battle and the whole congregation.
You shall take a tribute for the Lord from all the warriors who went out to battle: one in every five hundred, from the people, the livestock, the cattle, the sheep, and the goats.
And you shall take their half and give it to Eleazar the priest as the Lord’s offering.

And from the Israelites’ half you shall take one out of fifty, of the people and the livestock—the cattle, the sheep, the donkeys, and all the livestock—and give it to the Levites who attend to the duties of the Lord’s tabernacle.”
And Moses and Eleazar the priest did as the Lord had commanded Moses.
And the remainder of the spoils that the fighting men had brought as plunder was 675,000 sheep,
72,000 cattle,
61,000 donkeys,
and, among the women who had not known sexual relations with a man, 32,000 people in all.
And the half of the spoils belonging to those who went to battle numbered 337,500 sheep.
And the Lord’s share of the sheep was 675.
And 36,000 cattle, and the Lord’s share was seventy-two.
And 30,500 donkeys, and the Lord’s share was sixty-one.
The people numbered sixteen thousand, and the tribute to the Lord from them was thirty-two people.
And Moses gave the Lord’s share, the offering to God, to Eleazar the priest, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
The half belonging to the children of Israel, which Moses separated from the fighting men.
And the half belonging to the people amounted to 337,500 sheep,
and 36,000 cattle.
And thirty thousand five hundred donkeys.
And sixteen thousand people.

And Moses took from the half belonging to the children of Israel one out of every fifty, both people and animals, and gave them to the Levites who kept charge of the Lord’s tabernacle, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
And all the officers over the army’s divisions of a thousand, the commanders of thousands and the commanders of hundreds, approached Moses.
And they said to Moses, “Your servants have counted the fighting men under our command, and not one of them has been lost.
And we have brought an offering to present to the Lord, each man whatever gold he has found—a [?] or bracelets, a ring, a [?], or an interwoven [?]—to make atonement for ourselves before the Lord.”
And Moses and Eleazar the priest received the gold from them, all the crafted objects.
And all the gold of the contribution that they offered to the Lord amounted to 16,750 shekels, from the commanders of thousands.
And the fighting men who brought plunder, each for himself.

And Moses and Eleazar the priest received the gold from the commanders of thousands and the commanders of hundreds, and brought it into the tabernacle of testimony as a memorial for the children of Israel before the Lord.

And the children of Israel, the children of Reuben and the children of Gad, had livestock in very great abundance. And they saw the land of Jazer and the land of Gilead, and the place was suitable for flocks.
And the children of Reuben and the children of Gad approached and said to Moses, to Eleazar the priest, and to the leaders of the people,
“Ataroth, Dibon, Jazer, Nimrah, Heshbon, Elealeh, Sebam, Nebo, and Beon—
the land that the Lord delivered into the hands of the children of Israel is a land suitable for raising livestock, and your servants have flocks.”
And they said, “If we have found favor in your sight, let that land be given to your servants as a possession, and do not make us cross the Jordan.”
And Moses said to the children of Gad and the children of Reuben, “Shall your brothers go to war while you remain here?
And why do you turn the hearts of the children of Israel away from crossing into the land that the Lord is going to give them?
Did your fathers not do the same when I sent them from Kadesh-barnea to inspect the land?
And they went up to the Valley of the Grape Cluster and inspected the land, and discouraged the hearts of the children of Israel so that they would not enter the land that the Lord had given them.
And the Lord became fiercely angry that day, and swore, saying,
‘Let the men who came out of Egypt, twenty years old and older, who know good and evil, not see the land that I swore to give to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, because they did not follow me.’
except Caleb son of Jephunneh, who was set apart, and Joshua son of Nun, because they followed the Lord.
And the Lord became fiercely angry with Israel and made them wander in the wilderness for forty years, until the whole generation that had done evil before the Lord had perished.
And now you have risen up in place of your fathers, a gathering of sinful men, to add once again to the Lord’s fierce anger against Israel.
For you have turned away from him, causing him once again to abandon you here in the wilderness, and you will act wickedly against all these people.
And they approached him and said, “Let us build pens for our sheep and our livestock, and towns for our families.

And we will arm ourselves before the Lord and go as an advance guard for the Israelites, until we have brought them each to their own place. Our families will live in fortified towns because of the inhabitants of the land.
And we will not return to our homes until the Israelites have each received their allotted inheritance.
And we will not receive an inheritance among them across the Jordan or beyond it, because we have our allotment on this side of the Jordan, to the east.”
And Moses said to them, “If you do as you have said, if you arm yourselves before the Lord for battle,
All your armed men shall cross the Jordan before the Lord until his enemy is destroyed before him.
and the land is subdued before the Lord, then you may return and be free of obligation before the Lord and toward Israel. This land will be yours as a possession before the Lord.
But if you do not do this, you will be found guilty before the Lord, and you will recognize your sins when troubles come upon you.
Build yourselves towns for your families and pens for your flocks, and do whatever you have promised with your own mouths.”
And the descendants of Reuben and the descendants of Gad spoke to Moses and said, “Your servants will do as you, our lord, have commanded us.
Our families, our wives, and all our livestock will remain in the towns of Gilead.”
Your servants shall cross over, armed and equipped for battle before the Lord, as you, lord, say.
And Moses brought Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the leaders of the ancestral houses of the tribes of Israel before them.

And Moses said to them, “If these descendants of Reuben and Gad cross the Jordan with you, all armed for battle before the Lord, and you take possession of the land, give them the land of Gilead as a possession.

But if they do not cross with you armed for battle before the Lord, bring their families, their wives, and their livestock ahead of you into the land of the Canaanites, and let them receive an inheritance with you in the land of the Canaanites.”
The descendants of Reuben and the descendants of Gad answered and said, “Whatever you, our lord, say to your servants, we will do.
We will cross over armed before the Lord into the land of the Canaanites, and you will give us possessions on this side of the Jordan.”

And Moses gave the descendants of Gad, the descendants of Reuben, and half the tribe of Manasseh, the descendants of Joseph, the kingdom of Sihon king of the Amorites and the kingdom of Og king of Bashan: the land and its towns with their boundaries, and the towns throughout the surrounding land.
And the descendants of Gad built Dibon, Ataroth, and Aroer,
and Shophan and Jazer, and raised them up,
and Nimrah and Beth-haran, fortified towns and pens for flocks.
And the descendants of Reuben built Heshbon, Elealeh, and Kiriathaim.
And Baal-meon, fortified all around, and Sibmah. They gave the cities they built names of their own choosing.
And the son of Machir son of Manasseh went to Gilead, captured it, and destroyed the Amorite who lived there.
Moses gave Gilead to Machir son of Manasseh, and he settled there.
Jair, a descendant of Manasseh, went and captured their towns and named them the Villages of Jair.
Nobah went and captured Kenath and its villages and named them Nobah after himself.
These are the camping places of the Israelites after they came out of the land of Egypt with their army under the leadership of Moses and Aaron.
Moses recorded their departures and their camping places at the Lord’s command, and these are the camping places along their journeys.
They set out from Rameses in the first month, on the fifteenth day of the first month. On the day after the Passover, the Israelites went out with a raised hand in the sight of all the Egyptians.
The Egyptians were burying all their dead whom the Lord had struck down—all the firstborn in the land of the Egyptians. The Lord had also carried out judgment against their gods.
The Israelites set out from Rameses and camped at Succoth.
They set out from Succoth and camped at Buthan, which is part of the wilderness.
They set out and camped at the entrance to Pi-hahiroth, which is opposite Baal-zephon, and they camped opposite Migdol.
They set out from opposite Pi-hahiroth and passed through the midst of the sea into the wilderness. They traveled for three days through the wilderness and camped at the Bitter Springs.
They set out from the Bitter Springs and came to Elim. At Elim there were twelve springs of water and seventy palm trees, and they camped there by the water.
They set out from Elim and camped on the shore of the Red Sea.
They set out from the Red Sea and camped in the wilderness of Sin.
They set out from the wilderness of Sin and camped at Dophkah.
They set out from Dophkah and camped at Alush.
They set out from Alush and camped at Rephidim, and there was no water for the people to drink.
They set out from Rephidim and camped in the wilderness of Sinai.
They set out from the wilderness of Sinai and camped at the Graves of Craving.
They set out from the Graves of Craving and camped at Hazeroth.
They set out from Hazeroth and camped at Rithmah.
They set out from Rithmah and camped at Rimmon-perez.
They set out from Rimmon-perez and camped at Libnah.
They set out from Libnah and camped at Rissah.
They set out from Rissah and camped at Kehelathah.
They set out from Kehelathah and camped at Shapher.
They set out from Shapher and camped at Haradah.
They set out from Haradah and camped at Makheloth.
They set out from Makheloth and camped at Tahath.
They set out from Tahath and camped at Terah.
They set out from Terah and camped at Mithkah.
They set out from Mithkah and camped at Hashmonah.
They set out from Hashmonah and camped at Moseroth.
They set out from Moseroth and camped at Bene-jaakan.
They set out from Bene-jaakan and camped at Mount Gidgad.
They set out from Mount Gidgad and camped at Jotbathah.
They set out from Jotbathah and camped at Abronah.
They set out from Abronah and camped at Ezion-geber.
They set out from Ezion-geber and camped in the wilderness of Zin. They set out from the wilderness of Zin and camped in the wilderness of Paran, that is, Kadesh.
They set out from Kadesh and camped at Mount Hor, near the land of Edom.
Aaron the priest went up the mountain at the Lord’s command and died there in the fortieth year after the Israelites came out of the land of Egypt, in the fifth month, on the first day of the month.
Aaron was one hundred and twenty-three years old when he died on Mount Hor.
The Canaanite king of Arad heard when the Israelites were coming in; he was living in the land of the Canaanites.
They set out from Mount Hor and camped at Zalmonah.
They set out from Zalmonah and camped at Punon.
They set out from Punon and camped at Oboth.
They set out from Oboth and camped at Iye-abarim, beyond the borders of Moab.
They set out from Iye-abarim and camped at Dibon-gad.
They set out from Dibon-gad and camped at Almon-diblathaim.
They set out from Almon-diblathaim and camped in the mountains of Abarim, opposite Nebo.
They set out from the mountains of Abarim and camped on the western side of Moab, beside the Jordan, opposite Jericho.
They camped along the Jordan, from Beth-jeshimoth to Abel-shittim, on the western side of Moab.
The Lord spoke to Moses on the western side of Moab, beside the Jordan, opposite Jericho, and said:
Speak to the Israelites and say to them: You are now crossing the Jordan into the land of the Canaanites.
You shall destroy all the inhabitants of the land before you, demolish the lookout towers of their land, destroy all their cast idols, and remove all their pillars from among you.
You shall destroy the inhabitants of the land and settle in it yourselves, for I have given you their land as your allotted possession.

According to your tribes, you shall increase the possessions of those who are numerous and decrease the possessions of those who are few. Wherever the allotment falls in someone's name, there it shall be. You shall inherit according to your ancestral tribes.

But if you do not destroy the inhabitants of the land before you, those whom you leave will become obstacles in your eyes and arrows in your sides, and they will be your enemies in the land where you settle.
And what I planned to do to them, I will do to you.
And the Lord spoke to Moses and said:
Command the Israelites and say to them: You are entering the land of the Canaanites, and the land of Canaan, with its boundaries, shall be your inheritance.
Your southern side shall extend from the wilderness of Zin to the vicinity of Edom, and your southern boundary shall begin at the eastern end of the Salt Sea.

Your boundary shall turn southward along the ascent of Akrabbim and pass through Enak. Its endpoint shall be south of Kadesh-barnea, and it shall extend to the settlement of Arad and pass through Azmon.
The boundary shall turn from Azmon toward the ravine of Egypt, and its endpoint shall be at the sea.
Your sea boundary shall be the Great Sea. This shall be your sea boundary.
This shall be your northern boundary: from the Great Sea you shall mark out the mountain range for yourselves.
From that mountain you shall mark it out as far as the entrance to Hamath, and the boundary's endpoint shall be at Zedad.
It shall extend along the boundaries of Ziphron, and its endpoint shall be Hazar-enan. This shall be your northern boundary.
You shall mark out your eastern boundary from Hazar-enan to Shepham.
The boundary shall descend from Shepham to Bela, east of the springs, and descend from Bela as far as the eastern side of the Sea of Chinnereth.
The boundary shall descend to the Jordan, and its endpoint shall be the Salt Sea. All this land shall be yours, with its boundaries all around.
Moses commanded the Israelites and said: This is the land that you shall inherit by lot, as the Lord commanded it to be given to the nine tribes and the half-tribe of Manasseh.
For the tribe of the descendants of Reuben and the tribe of the descendants of Gad, according to their ancestral households, and half the tribe of Manasseh have received their allotments
beyond the Jordan, opposite Jericho, on the south toward the east.
And the Lord spoke to Moses and said:
These are the names of the men who shall assign the land to you as an inheritance: Eleazar the priest and Joshua son of Nun.
You shall take one leader from each tribe to assign the land to you as an inheritance.
These are the names of the men: from the tribe of Judah, Caleb son of Jephunneh;
from the tribe of Simeon, Shelumiel son of Ammihud;
from the tribe of Benjamin, Eldad son of Chislon.
For the tribe of Dan, the leader was Bukki son of Jogli.
For the descendants of Joseph, for the tribe of the descendants of Manasseh, the leader was Hanniel son of Suphi.
For the tribe of the descendants of Ephraim, the leader was Kemuel son of Shabbethai.
For the tribe of Zebulun, the leader was Elizaphan son of Parnach.
For the tribe of the descendants of Issachar, the leader was Paltiel son of Uzziah.
For the tribe of the descendants of Asher, the leader was Achior son of Shelomi.
For the tribe of Naphtali, the leader was Pedahel son of Ammihud.
These are the men whom the Lord commanded to divide the land of the Canaanites among the Israelites.
And the Lord spoke to Moses in the western region of Moab, beside the Jordan, opposite Jericho, saying:
Command the Israelites to give the Levites cities to live in from their allotted landholdings, and to give the Levites pasturelands around their cities.
The cities shall be theirs to live in, and the lands set apart for them shall be for their flocks and all their four-footed animals.
The outlying lands of the cities that you give the Levites shall extend two thousand cubits all around, from the city wall outward.

Outside the city, you shall measure two thousand cubits on the eastern side, two thousand cubits on the southern side, two thousand cubits on the western side, and two thousand cubits on the northern side, with the city in the middle. These shall be the pasturelands of the cities for you.
Among the cities that you give the Levites shall be the six cities of refuge, which you shall provide so that a killer may flee there, and in addition to these, forty-two cities.
In all, you shall give the Levites forty-eight cities, together with their pasturelands.

As for the cities that you give from the Israelites’ landholdings, take many from those who have much and few from those who have little. Each shall give cities to the Levites in proportion to the inheritance they receive.
And the Lord spoke to Moses and said:
Speak to the Israelites and say to them: You are about to cross the Jordan into the land of the Canaanites.
Set apart cities for yourselves to serve as places of refuge, so that a killer—anyone who unintentionally strikes someone dead—may flee there.
These cities shall be a refuge for you from the avenger of blood, so that the killer will not die before standing before the congregation for judgment.
The cities that you provide shall be six cities of refuge for you.
You shall provide three cities on the other side of the Jordan and three cities in the land of the Canaanites, and they shall serve as a refuge.
For the Israelites, the newcomer, and the foreigner living among you, these six cities shall be places of refuge, so that anyone who unintentionally strikes someone dead may flee there.
If someone strikes another with an iron tool and kills him, he is a murderer; the murderer shall surely be put to death.
If someone strikes another with a stone held in the hand that can cause death, and he dies, he is a murderer; the murderer shall surely be put to death.
If someone strikes another with a wooden tool held in the hand that can cause death, and he dies, he is a murderer; the murderer shall surely be put to death.
The avenger of blood shall kill the murderer; when he encounters him, he shall kill him.
If he pushes him out of hatred, or throws any object at him with malicious intent, and he dies,

Or if he strikes him with his own hand out of [?], and he dies, the one who struck him must be put to death; he is a murderer. The one they put to death must be put to death. The next of kin shall kill the murderer when he encounters him.
But if he pushes him accidentally and not out of hostility, or throws any object at him without malicious intent,
or strikes him unknowingly with any stone capable of causing death, and he dies, although he was not his enemy and did not seek to harm him,
the community shall judge between the one who struck him and the next of kin according to these judgments.

The congregation shall rescue the killer from the avenger of blood, and the congregation shall send him back to the city of refuge where he had taken shelter. He shall live there until the death of the high priest who was anointed with the holy oil.
But if the killer goes beyond the boundaries of the city to which he fled for refuge,
and the next of kin finds him outside the boundaries of his city of refuge, and the next of kin kills the killer, he shall not be liable to death.
For this reason, he shall live in his city of refuge until the death of the high priest. After the death of the high priest, the killer may return to the land of his own possession.
This shall be a legal statute for you throughout your generations, wherever you live.
Whoever strikes a person, the killer shall be put to death on the testimony of witnesses. A single witness shall not testify so as to have a person put to death.
You shall not accept a ransom for the life of a murderer who is liable to death; he must be put to death.
You shall not accept a ransom for someone who has fled to a city of refuge to return and live in the land before the high priest dies.
You shall not defile the land, and the land cannot be cleansed of the blood shed upon it except by the shedding of blood.
You shall not pollute the land in which you live, where I will dwell among you, for I am the Lord God who dwells among the children of Israel.

The leaders of the clan of the descendants of Gilead, son of Machir, son of Manasseh, from the tribe of the descendants of Joseph, approached and spoke before Moses, before Eleazar the priest, and before the leaders of the ancestral houses of the children of Israel.

They said, “The Lord commanded our lord to give the land to the children of Israel as an inheritance by lot, and the Lord commanded our lord to give the inheritance of our brother Zelophehad to his daughters.

Now, if they become wives of men from one of the tribes of Israel, their allotted share will be taken from the possessions of our fathers and added to the inheritance of the tribe whose men they marry. It will be taken from our allotted inheritance.

And when the Jubilee comes for the children of Israel, their inheritance will be added to the inheritance of the tribe whose men they marry, and their inheritance will be taken from the inheritance of our ancestral tribe.”
Moses instructed the children of Israel at the Lord’s command and spoke in response to what the tribe of the descendants of Joseph had said to him:
“This is what the Lord commanded concerning the daughters of Zelophehad: They may marry those who seem pleasing in their eyes, but they must marry within their father’s tribe.
The inheritance of the children of Israel shall not pass from tribe to tribe, for the children of Israel shall each hold fast to the ancestral inheritance of their own tribe.

Every young woman entitled to an inheritance among the tribes of the children of Israel shall marry someone from her father’s clan, so that the children of Israel may each possess their own ancestral inheritance.
An allotted share shall not pass from one tribe to another; rather, the children of Israel shall each hold fast to their own inheritance.”
The daughters of Zelophehad did as the Lord had commanded Moses.
Tirzah, Hoglah, Milcah, Noah, and Mahlah, the daughters of Zelophehad, married the sons of their paternal uncles.
They married within the tribe of Manasseh, son of Joseph, and their inheritances remained within their father’s clan.
These are the commandments, statutes, and judgments that the Lord commanded through Moses in western Moab, beside the Jordan, opposite Jericho.
